title: 'I knew this was the end of my career': Doval recalls when China captured his agents
author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
text:
NEW DELHI: National security advisor 
Ajit Doval
 on Saturday recalled one of the most difficult moments of his early career, when a group of operatives sent across the border went missing and were later found to be in Chinese custody.
Speaking as the chief guest at the two-day convocation ceremony of IIT Roorkee, NSA Doval said he was deeply worried after receiving no information about the group's whereabouts.
He said: âWe got no reports of any avalanche or anything. It was a matter of deep worry and concern. But I got a telephone call from the headquarters, and my boss told me, "Have you sent some people across?" I said, "I do not know. They must be coming. They should have come in five or six days, but now it is about ten or eleven days." He said, "They are in Chinese custody now." They were caught by the Chinese and interrogated. Anyway, the Chinese returned them, probably after some talks or negotiations, or a deal must have been struck. So, they returned totally shattered, in shambles. And an inquiry was started. I knew that this was the end of my career. I was still in my twenties, and I had to start a new career. 
I saw the incident as something very unprofessional.â
Doval said an inquiry was later conducted and he was not held responsible for the incident.
âAnyway, the inquiry was over. I wasn't found at fault. Probably, I had done everything right. The sketches and the maps that were given to us by the headquarters had some defects and mistakes in them. That is how it happened," the NSA added.

Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines
He also spoke about the opportunities available to today's younger generation, particularly with rapid advances in technology.
"You may not be conscious of the fact that in the last 1000 years, you are the luckiest generation, which is going to have so many opportunities. Generations before you were struggling under slavery. They did not have those opportunities which opened up for you. And not only that, things have changed here, but globally things have changed for the better for you... You are coming at an age when technology will be the most important driving factor in any country's or society's growth and progress," Ajit Doval said.
The two-day convocation began at IIT Roorkee on Saturday, with degrees set to be awarded to 2,701 students. NSA Doval attended the event as the chief guest.

title: 'How is it possible?' Kejriwal and family get SIR notice in Delhi, EC responds
author: AADRITA HALDER
text:
NEW DELHI: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief and former Delhi chief minister 
Arvind Kejriwal
 and four members of his family have been served notices by the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office under the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Notices have been issued to Kejriwal, his wife Sunita Kejriwal, son Pulkit Kejriwal, and parents Gobind Ram Kejriwal and 
Gita Devi
. Kejriwal is a registered voter in the New Delhi-40 assembly constituency.
According to Delhi Election Commission documents, Arvind Kejriwal and five members of his family are among 110 voters from âPart-51, KG Margâ in the New Delhi assembly constituency who have been issued notices.
The party questioned the move saying, âIs everything happening in this country just to keep the Supreme Lord happy? @ECISVEEP, how is it possible that the names of three-time Delhi Chief Minister @ArvindKejriwal Ji and his family members are missing from the Delhi voter list?â
AAP questions names missing from voter list
EC responds to Kejriwal's SIR notice
The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), New Delhi, has said notices were issued to former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and his family members as their submitted Enumeration Forms did not contain sufficient details to establish their linkage with the electoral rolls of the last revision in their respective states.
The ERO said, âthe submitted Enumeration Forms were not complete in terms of details which would have enabled linkage of themselves with the electoral roll of the last revision of the respective states, which were not present in their submitted Enumeration Forms.â
In a press statement, the ERO further said that notices were being issued in accordance with procedures established and communicated by the Election Commission to electors who could not be linked to the electoral roll of the last revision or whose linkage showed logical discrepancies.
â As per procedures established and communicated by ECI, Notices are being issued to the electors who could not be linked with the electoral roll of the last revision and those having logical discrepancies in their linking with the electoral roll of the last revision. Electors have to submit a reply/requisite documents to the ERO concerned on receipt of the Notice. Disposal of Notices will be completed by 29.10.2026,â the statement said.
The Election Commission also said a notice was issued to Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta after her name appeared in the list of discrepancies during the ongoing SIR process.
Following verification of her details and documents, her electoral entry was validated and will be included in the final electoral roll for AC-14 (Shalimar Bagh), scheduled to be published on November 4, 2026.
The notices come amid the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2026 exercise being conducted by the Delhi Election Commission. Nearly 47.6 lakh names were removed from Delhi's draft electoral roll published on August 31, but only a fraction of those affected have so far submitted Form 6 seeking re-inclusion.
The window for filing claims and objections against the draft roll will remain open until September 30.
The draft electoral roll contains 97.5 lakh electors, compared with 1.45 crore registered voters in Delhi when the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise began in June.
Data showed that 62,583 Form 6 applications, including those from first-time voters seeking inclusion, had been submitted by September 15. The number rose to 68,043 by September 16.
The 47.6 lakh electors excluded from Delhi's draft electoral roll have been categorised as Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others following the house-to-house verification exercise. Around 43.3 lakh were marked as absent or shifted, while about 2.8 lakh were categorised as dead and 1.4 lakh as duplicate entries.

According to figures released by the Delhi election office for the claims and objections phase, 91,826 applications were received between August 31 and September 16.
These included 22,715 Form 8 applications seeking correction or modification of existing electoral entries, 922 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names on grounds such as death, shifting, duplicate registration or ineligibility, and 146 Form 6A applications from overseas electors, besides Form 6 applications for inclusion in the electoral roll.
After the claims and objections phase ends, officials will examine the applications and complete the disposal process by October 29. The final electoral roll under the SIR exercise is scheduled to be published on November 4.

title: IIT-Bombay suicide: Parents refuse to take son's body; crime branch to probe case
author: TNN
text:
MUMBAI: The probe in the abetment of suicide case of an IIT-Bombay student was transferred to the 
Mumbai Police
's crime branch late on Saturday.
An ACP-rank officer from the crime branch will be carrying out the probe.
Sahil Wakode, 20, was found dead in his hostel room at the campus on Friday.
After his parents lodged a complaint with the Powai Police on Saturday, an FIR was registered for abetment of suicide under provisions of Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
Police also applied provisions of the 
Prevention of Atrocities Act
, after Wakode's parents complained that he was being harassed with "casteist slurs."
The FIR names a senior professor of 
IIT Bombay
 besides "other senior officials."
This is the third incident of suicide on the campus this year.
Wakodeâs parents, Ravindra, an office-bearer with a multipurpose cooperative society, and Sonali, a govt school teacher, refused to claim their sonâs body from the post-mortem centre at Rajawadi Hospital for over seven hours on Saturday.
âI will not conduct the final rites of my son till the accused persons are arrested,â said Ravindra.
Wakode was their only child. As the standoff continued, senior IPS officers reached the hospital and tried to persuade the couple to claim the body, assuring them that action would be taken on their complaint.
The body was claimed around 9pm after the case was transferred to the crime branch.
An IIT-Bombay spokesperson said that the police have registered a case and the matter is under investigation and that IIT-Bombay will cooperate fully with the authorities and requested everyone to respect the familyâs privacy.
âWe ask that people refrain from speculation as the investigation proceeds,â the spokesperson added.

title: Father-son duo makes history: Shigenobu and Koji light cauldron in Nagoya
author: AMIT KUMAR
text:
A father and son who built their legacy in hammer throw shared one of the biggest moments of the 
Asian Games
 opening ceremony on Saturday.
Japanâs Shigenobu Murofushi and his son Koji Murofushi jointly lit the cauldron at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, bringing the torch relay to a memorable end.
Both Shigenobu and Koji are former Asian Games champions in hammer throw. The duo climbed the stairs to the podium together before lighting the cauldron.
The ceremony featured dance, music and fireworks as the Asian Games officially opened in Aichi-Nagoya.
From Olympic champion to father-son moment
The cauldron lighting was the final part of a relay involving some of Japanâs biggest sporting names.
Womenâs wrestler Fujinami Akari brought the torch into the stadium before passing it to four-time Olympic swimming champion Kitajima Kosuke.
The torch then went to Ito Koji, a three-time gold medallist in athletics at the 1998 Bangkok Asian Games. Takahashi Ayaka, the 2016 Rio Olympics badminton womenâs doubles champion, was next.
Shigenobu Murofushi and Koji Murofushi (Reuters Photo)
The torch was then handed to Koji Murofushi, the 2004 Athens Olympics hammer throw champion.
The final torchbearer was his father, Shigenobu Murofushi, who won the Asian Games hammer throw title five times in a row.
The two then came together to light the cauldron, which had a metallic design inspired by the shape of a heart.
Who is Shigenobu Murofushi?
Shigenobu Murofushi is one of Japanâs most successful hammer throwers. He competed at three Olympic Games â Munich 1972, Montreal 1976 and Los Angeles 1984.
He also served as Japanâs flag-bearer at the 1984 Olympics.
Murofushi initially tried sumo and shot put before taking up hammer throw. In 1984, he set a Japanese record of 75.96m. That mark remained the national record until his son Koji broke it in 1998.
Shigenobu won the Asian Games hammer throw gold medal in 1970, 1974, 1978, 1982 and 1986. He also won silver in 1966.
His Asian Games medal record includes five gold medals and one silver.
He also won gold at the 1979 and 1981 Asian Championships.
Shigenobuâs Olympic journey
While Shigenobu dominated the Asian Games, an Olympic medal remained out of reach.
He finished eighth at the 1972 Munich Olympics, 11th at Montreal 1976 and 15th at Los Angeles 1984.
His son would later achieve what he could not at the Olympics.
Koji Murofushi followed his fatherâs footsteps
Koji started hammer throw at the age of 10 under the guidance of his father.
He went on to become one of the leading hammer throwers in the world. Koji won the silver medal at the 2001 World Championships before claiming bronze in 2003.
His biggest Olympic moment came at the 2004 Athens Games, where he won the hammer throw gold medal.
He added an Olympic bronze at the 2012 London Games.
Koji also became world champion in 2011 in Daegu.
Shigenobu Murofushi and Koji Murofushi (Reuters Photo)
Kojiâs Asian Games medal record
Koji continued his familyâs success at the Asian Games.
He won gold in hammer throw at Bangkok in 1998 and Busan in 2002. He had earlier won silver at Hiroshima in 1994.
His Asian Games record therefore includes two gold medals and one silver.
Koji also won gold at the 2002 Asian Championships and three silver medals at the continental championships in 1993, 1995 and 1998.
A family legacy comes full circle
The Murofushis have now added another special chapter to their long sporting legacy.
Shigenobu dominated the Asian Games in the 1970s and 1980s. Koji followed him into the event and later became an Olympic and world champion.
On Saturday, the father and son stood together at the centre of the Asian Games opening ceremony â not to compete, but to light the flame that officially began the Games.
Glittering opening ceremony
The 20th Asian Games officially began in Nagoya with a two-hour opening ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium. Japan's Emperor Naruhito officially declared the Games open. Empress Masako, members of the Japanese imperial family, Olympic Council of Asia president Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani and International Olympic Committee president Kirsty Coventry were also present at the ceremony.
The event started with the Japanese national anthem and the raising of the national flag. Nine members of the Japanese Self-Defence Forces carried the flag to the stage before it was hoisted.
The stadium was then turned dark, with a spotlight focused on the Japanese flag.
The ceremony was followed by the parade of athletes. Teams from 45 nations and regions took part, along with the OCA Refugee Team, taking the total number of participating delegations to 46.

title: A Tulu promise: Why DKS is trying a different language in BJP's coastal bastion
author: KARAN MANRAL
text:
NEW DELHI: 
Karnataka
 chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 on Friday announced that Tulu, spoken in the state's Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, would be recognised as an additional administrative language in the region, fulfilling a long-standing demand.
"Today, we have decided to make Tulu applicable to Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts and declare it the stateâs second additional administrative language," Shivakumar told reporters after a marathon cabinet meeting in Mangaluru.
According to a cabinet note shared by the chief ministerâs office, Tulu would be Karnatakaâs "second additional administrative language" in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi.
The 2011 national census recorded more than 18 lakh native Tulu speakers in Karnataka, whose population was recorded at over six crore at the time. Kannada is the state's most-widely spoken and its primary official language.
This was also the first time a cabinet meeting was held in Mangaluru and not in Bengaluru.
Eye on BJP's coastal bastion
The political significance of Shivakumar taking his cabinet to Mangaluru becomes clearer against the BJP's electoral dominance in the region.
Coastal Karnataka, particularly Dakshina Kannada and Udupi, has long been one of the BJP's strongest pockets in the state. 
In the 2023 Karnataka assembly election, BJP won 11 of the 13 seats across the two districts, taking all five seats in Udupi and six of the eight in Dakshina Kannada. The Congress won only two constituencies.
This was despite Congress sweeping to power across Karnataka with 135 seats, against 66 for the BJP.
The BJP's hold remained intact in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. It won both parliamentary seats covering the region, with Brijesh Chowta defeating Congress's Padmaraj R by over 64,000 votes in Dakshina Kannada. Kota Srinivas Poojary won Udupi-Chikkamagaluru by more than 2.5 lakh votes.
The BJP responded to the Tulu announcement by alleging that Shivakumar was "peddling soft Hindutva to make a dent in the BJPâs vote bank."
"Shivakumar has never made any secret of his firm belief in Hinduism and frequently visits temples, performs rituals publicly and quotes scriptures. He is now peddling soft Hindutva. This was also evident from his rendition of 'Namaste Sada Vatsale' inside the Karnataka assembly," a BJP leader told PTI, referring to an August 2025 incident in which Shivakumar sang a few lines of the RSS anthem.
The RSS is the BJP's ideological mentor.
But there is a political twist to the Tulu issue itself. The BJP had previously taken up the demand while in power in Karnataka.
In January 2023, the then BJP government led by Basavaraj Bommai constituted a committee to examine granting Tulu the status of a second official language in the state, months before the assembly election.
More than just Tulu
Significantly, Shivakumarâs announcements went beyond granting Tulu the status of a second administrative language.
The Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru marked the Shivakumar governmentâs first meeting outside Bengaluru, the state capital. Shivakumar claimed the move was intended to recognise the regionâs contribution and address its development needs.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines
The chief minister added that a draft notification would soon be issued to invite public feedback on renaming the Dakshina Kannada district to Mangaluru district.
He also announced a host of policies for the coastal Karnataka region, introducing a dedicated tourism policy for the coastal areas to treats tourism projects as infrastructure initiatives while offering investors special incentives and extended loan repayment windows.
Additionally, the government approved the Karnataka Marine Biotechnology Policy, 2026-31, which paves the way for upgrading the existing fisheries college into the Fisheries, Marine and Blue Economy University and expanding its student intake from 60 to 200 seats.
Beyond these policies, the administration unveiled new urban development planning, fisheries sector incentives, and major financial allocations totaling around Rs 32,611 croreâsplit evenly between rural development and regional growth for Mangaluru, Udupi, and the coastal region.
The announcements further included plans to hold decentralised Cabinet meetings across 10 to 12 locations in the state over the next 15 months and the sanctioning of a new medical college worth approximately Rs 450 crore for the region.

title: Atlanta man arrested after phone wipe; new ruling allows border searches
author: TOI TECH DESK
text:
An American citizen was arrested at Atlanta airport after his phone was wiped when he entered a PIN during an airport search in January this year. Months later, a new US court ruling has highlighted just how much power border authorities have when it comes to searching travellersâ electronic devices. The January case of Atlanta resident Samuel Tunick involved GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused Android operating system that has a feature allowing users to wipe a phone with a designated PIN. Prosecutors accused Tunick of destroying potential evidence. His lawyers have challenged the search and the seizure of his phone.
Now, the US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit has ruled in a separate case that border agents can search a travellerâs cellphone without reasonable suspicion or a warrant. The ruling was issued on September 17 in United States v. Alisigwe. As stated in a Bloomberg report, the decision does not concern Tunick or GrapheneOS directly. But it comes after the July case and adds to the debate around phone privacy, airport searches and electronic device searches at the US border.
What happened at Atlanta airport in January
Samuel Tunick was returning from the Dominican Republic when federal agents stopped him at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on January 24, according to the case details you provided. 
The agents repeatedly asked him to unlock his phone and warned that it could be seized if he refused. After he entered a PIN, his phone reportedly went blank, flashed several times and appeared to restart. The data stored on the device was then lost.
Prosecutors alleged that Tunick deliberately wiped the phone to prevent authorities from accessing potential evidence. His lawyers then argued that the underlying search was unlawful and sought to have the case dismissed. They also disputed the government's account of the incident.
What does the new US court ruling say about phone searches
The new ruling comes from the Second Circuit, which covers New York, Connecticut and Vermont. The case involved Chinwendu Alisigwe, a lawful permanent resident whose cellphone was searched by federal agents at John F. Kennedy International Airport in 2019 and again in 2021. Agents manually went through the phone and photographed information found on it.
Alisigwe argued that the searches violated the Fourth Amendment because the government did not have a warrant. The appeals court rejected that argument.
The court held that border agents do not need reasonable suspicion before manually searching a traveller's cellphone at the border. It said a cellphone is considered property for purposes of the existing border-search exception to the Fourth Amendment. The court also rejected the argument that the First Amendment creates a separate warrant requirement for cellphone searches at the border.
Does this mean US border agents can search any phone
While the ruling is significant, its exact scope matters. The Second Circuit's decision concerns border searches of travellers' electronic devices. It does not mean police can generally search any person's phone anywhere in the US without legal restrictions.
The court relied on the long-standing border-search exception, under which the government has broad authority to inspect people and property entering the country. The court said this authority extends to cellphones and that reasonable suspicion is not required for the type of manual cellphone search involved in the case.
Judge Eunice Lee agreed with the result but wrote separately. She questioned the majority's broader conclusion that cellphone searches should be treated as routine searches requiring no suspicion, noting the amount of highly private information stored on modern phones.
What about laptops and other electronic devices
The ruling specifically concerned cellphone searches. The court's reasoning relies on the border-search exception and the treatment of a cellphone as property. So the headline question around phone and laptop searches needs some care: the decision does not specifically establish a separate rule for every type of electronic device in every situation.
The broader legal issue is whether electronic devices carried across an international border receive special protection from warrantless searches. In this case, the Second Circuit said the Fourth Amendment does not require a warrant or reasonable suspicion for the cellphone search at issue.
Why the July GrapheneOS case matters
The Tunick case and the Alisigwe ruling involve different people, different airports and different legal proceedings. But both involve a growing question for travellers: what happens to the data on a phone when US authorities want to inspect it at the border?
In Tunick's case, prosecutors allege that wiping the phone interfered with their ability to obtain evidence. In Alisigwe, the appeals court addressed the government's authority to search a cellphone in the first place. The two cases therefore highlight different sides of the same broader issue: government access to smartphones at international borders and the privacy protections available to travellers.

title: ‘Arrogance of power’: Congress calls out Scindia over his viral video
author: SUBHADRA SRIVASTAVA
text:
Union minister's fiery response to Guna resident goes viral, Congress reacts
NEW DELHI: A video showing Union minister Jyotiraditya M Scindia in a sharp exchange with a resident over a long-pending road in Guna, Madhya Pradesh, has gone viral on social media, with the Congress sharing the clip and accusing the minister of showing âarrogance of powerâ.
The party also alleged that Scindia âflew into a rageâ. The party added, âThe moment the public demanded a road, 'His Majesty' flew into a rage.â It further quoted Scindiaâs response and said, âThe public will soon put this arrogance in its place.â
Subhadra Srivastava is a journalist with The Times of India, covering geopolitics, international and national affairs. With over three years of experience, she focuses on national and global developments, conflict, diplomacy and their impact on India. Her work combines breaking news with in-depth analysis, offering readers context and clarity on the stories shaping the world.

title: UPI MDR: Can Rs 6,000 be split into three Rs 2,000 payments? No daily cap
author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
text:
From October 15, 2026, 
UPI
 payments above Rs 2,000 made to large merchants will attract a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) of 0.4%. However, the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) reportedly does not currently plan to introduce a separate daily limit on repeated UPI payments made to the same merchant.
Such a restriction, if in place, could prevent businesses from breaking up larger payments into multiple transactions of Rs 2,000 or less.
No daily cap on UPI right now
Under the framework that will take effect from October 15, regular merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 will attract a 0.4% merchant discount rate, with the charge capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 or more.
For example, a merchant receiving a single UPI payment of Rs 6,000 would incur an MDR of Rs 24.
However, according to an ET report, instead of making one payment, the merchant could ask the customer to make three separate payments of Rs 2,000 each. Since each transaction would fall within the free limit, the merchant could avoid the Rs 24 charge, industry executives told the financial daily.
The NPCI framework and the FAQs issued with it do not stipulate that multiple payments relating to a single bill must be clubbed together.
âIf the customer is willing to pay the merchant three times and both sides agree, it is between them. There is not much that can be done at the transaction level,â one person directly involved with NPCI told the financial daily. They also did not expect such workarounds to become significant over time.
Zero MDR loophole
Another potential gap relates to the zero-MDR person-to-person-merchant (P2PM) category available to small merchants. Banks and payment service providers track the UPI collections of merchants in this category and shift them to the regular merchant category if their collections cross Rs 1 lakh a month for three consecutive months.
The FAQs do not clarify whether a merchantâs collections have to be aggregated across different bank accounts, QR codes or payment service providers.
Industry executives said merchants could potentially distribute their receipts across these channels to keep each one below the prescribed threshold. Detecting such arrangements effectively would require linking the different accounts and payment channels to the same business.
Another possible workaround would be to direct business payments to personal UPI IDs, since person-to-person transactions continue to remain free regardless of the amount.
However, doing so would effectively present commercial receipts as personal transfers rather than using a legitimate exemption. Banks or payment providers could subsequently reclassify the account.
Businesses could also gain from being incorrectly assigned to a merchant category that attracts a flat Rs 5 charge instead of the 0.4% rate.
Railways, telecom services, insurance, fuel and utilities are among the categories eligible for concessional charges. Merchant category codes are assigned when a business is onboarded, and deliberately providing an incorrect classification would therefore amount to a breach of the rules, industry executives said.
Genuine recurring UPI AutoPay transactions are exempt from the charges. However, executives said treating an ordinary sale as a recurring payment merely to claim the exemption would constitute misclassification.
People familiar with the matter said NPCI expects some merchants to explore these workarounds once the new framework comes into effect. However, it does not currently believe additional transaction-level limits are necessary. The payments body also does not expect merchants splitting bills to become widespread or continue as a significant practice over the longer term.
More than 95% of merchant-payment volumes will continue to remain free under the framework. At the same time, industry estimates show that transactions above Rs 2,000 represent around two-thirds of the total value of merchant payments. This means widespread attempts to avoid the charges could have a meaningful impact on the collections expected under the new system.
NPCI has said the MDR revenue will be used to support UPI infrastructure, cybersecurity and customer service.

title: Thane man slams 2-year-old son on floor, scalds hand on hot plate for 'ignoring' him
author: PRACHI KUMAWAT
text:
THANE: A Kalyan man allegedly assaulted his two-year-old son after becoming enraged when the toddler avoided him at home, slamming the child to the floor and pressing his hand against a hot plate, leaving three fingers scalded, police said on Saturday.
The man also allegedly assaulted his wife when she intervened to protect their child.
Accused Rahul Suresh Visale and his wife Rohini, residents of Parnaka in Kalyan West, have been embroiled in marital disputes, with one matter previously reaching the court, a Bazarpeth police station official said.
According to Rohini's complaint, the incident took place around 11pm on September 13 when Visale allegedly became enraged after seeing the child avoid him and slammed him on the floor, the official said.
"Visale pressed then pressed the child's hand on a hot plate, resulting in three of the child's fingers getting scalded. The accused also assaulted Rohini when she intervened to protect her child. She was hit with a broom," he said.
The official said the couple had been facing marital disputes and that a matter had earlier reached the court. The court recently advised Rohini to live with her husband for two months in an attempt to reconcile.
Following the court's direction, Rohini moved back to her husband's residence in Parnaka from her parents' home, he said.
In her complaint, Rohini alleged that her husband harboured resentment over their past disputes, which led to the assault on her and their child, the official said.
Visale was booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act. He is yet to be arrested, the official added.
(With PTI inputs)

title: 'We want to go home': Hindu minor sisters abducted, converted, married in Pakistan
author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
text:
The alleged abduction and forced conversion of two minor Hindu sisters in Pakistan's Sindh province has triggered fresh concern among minority rights group, with one organisation calling for an independent probe and safeguards for the girls.
According to Voice of Pakistan Minority, Roopi, 13 and Seeta, 14, were allegedly taken from Ibrahim Colony in Tando Allahyar district and later converted to Islam and married to two Muslim men, Amjad Solangi and Mansood Solangi.
The sisters were subsequently brought before a court in Tando Allahyar in an abduction case. Instead of sending them back to their family, the court placed them in a safe house, VOPM said.
The rights group said the girls appeared distressed outside the court and were heard pleading to be taken home. A video circulating online also purportedly showed the sisters saying, âLet us go to our parentsâ and âWe want to go home.â
VOPM said the circumstances surrounding the case made it important that the sisters be heard independently, without anyone who could influence or intimidate them.
âThe state must interview Roopi and Seeta in a child-sensitive environment, away from alleged husbands, religious figures, intermediaries or anyone who could pressure them. 
Officials must allow the girls to speak freely and must provide them independent legal support and protection,â VOPM said.
The organisation called for an urgent, independent and transparent investigation into the allegations.
Sindh at centre of concern over minority girls
The case has also renewed attention on the vulnerability of Hindu families in Sindh, which has Pakistan's largest Hindu population. VOPM said the problem is particularly acute in rural areas, where poverty, caste discrimination and limited access to legal assistance can leave minority families vulnerable.
âThis case has caused deep anxiety among Hindu communities in Sindh. Sindh hosts Pakistanâs largest Hindu population, particularly in rural districts where many Hindu families face poverty, caste discrimination and weak access to legal help,â it said.
Rights groups have for years raised concerns over allegations involving the abduction, conversion and marriage of minority girls in Pakistan.
VOPM cited data from the Centre for Social Justice, included in UK government material, which recorded 421 such cases involving minority girls and women between 2021 and 2024. Hindu women and girls accounted for 282 of those cases, while 72 per cent were reported from Sindh.
The organisation said Pakistani authorities recorded at least 83 cases in 2024 alone, with Hindu girls making up 63 per cent of the victims.
The concern extends beyond the figures. VOPM also referred to warnings by UN experts in 2026 that nearly 80 per cent of reported cases involving alleged forced conversion through marriage in Pakistan during 2025 took place in Sindh. About 75 per cent of the victims were reportedly Hindus.
For VOPM, the immediate focus remains on the two sisters and whether they can speak freely about what happened to them.
âRoopi and Seetaâs reported call to return home demands attention. Their protection, age, dignity, and freedom must come before every other consideration,â the VOPM noted.

title: Invasive spotted lanternfly reaches Canada after spreading across 18 US states
author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
text:
Canada has recently confirmed the first detection of spotted lanternfly in the country. On September 15, 2026, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) confirmed the first detection of SLF in Canada in Windsor, Ontario. Movement restrictions have been placed to prevent the movement of regulated materials, including potentially infested plant materials. Moreover, surrounding areas are under surveillance to determine the extent of the infestation and the next steps.
Spotted lanternflies are considered an invasive species in South Korea and the United States. A species is invasive when itâs introduced, often unintentionally by people, to a non-native area and spreads, frequently causing harm to the new environment.
They were first reported as an introduced species in Korea in 1932. However, itâs possible that this may have been a misidentification, as none were reported again until 2006, when they suddenly became a common sight.
In Japan, the insects may have occurred sporadically since the 1930s, but 2008 saw outbreaks of spotted lanternflies in Ishikawa Prefecture. It was first detected in Berks County in Pennsylvania, North America in 2014. 
has been regulated in Canada since 2018. It is known to feed on more than 100 species of trees and plants but significant impacts have been noticed on grapes and ultimately, the wine industry. This pest could also have an impact on other crop growers and the horticulture and forestry industries, as well as residential yards and neighbourhood parks. Spotted lanternfly can have widespread economic, ecological, and social impacts if allowed to spread uncontrolled.
âYou can help identify and report new invasive species, such as spotted lanternfly,â says Colin Cassin, Executive Director of the Invasive Species Centre. âThe earlier an invasive species is detected, the better the chances of reducing spread to other areas.â
How to offer community support?
Spotted lanternfly egg masses appear as grey smears of mud on host trees or any hard surface outdoors. They typically begin appearing in September and throughout winter until they hatch in spring. Early-stage nymphs are typically black with white spots; late-stage nymphs are red with black and white spots. Adults have pinkish-grey wings with black spots. Visible in spring and summer, they tend to congregate in swarms and ascend plants and trees to feed. They also congregate in large swarms on trees, grapevines, and other plants and may be seen from summer until they die in late fall/early winter. Adults are most active in September and October, when they are mating and laying eggs. Honeydew (clear, sticky liquid insect excrement) can accumulate at the base of a host tree. It can foster the growth of sooty mould and often attract bees and wasps.
In case you spot any of these, you need to take a photo or video and then put the insect or egg masses into a sealable plastic bag or container. All Canadians must report any suspect sightings of SLF to the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) immediately. A good report includes an accurate location and photos of the insect. The CFIA will follow up on reports of spotted lanternfly and take appropriate action, which may include site surveying and insect collection.
If you are travelling back from infested areas in US, it is important to check your car, camper, trailer or RV before making the return trip. Be sure to check any camping gear or equipment you have with you before returning to Canada.
Inspect items stored outside for egg masses, including your vehicle and patio furniture. Look closely at things like tarps, yard and garden items and sports equipment. Check your yard as well, as the spotted lanternfly could be on your trees and plants.
What's at risk?
Spotted lanternflies are known to cause severe agricultural damage by secreting sticky waste that grows black sooty mould. Most at risk are cultivated and wild grapes. Large swarms weaken vines, eliminate crop yields, lower winter hardiness, and can kill the plant entirely. Vineyards have reported up to a 90% loss in crop yield. In Pennsylvania alone, if the spotted lanternfly isnât contained, a 2019 study estimated that they could drain the stateâs economy by up to $324 million (Â£240 million) each year and cause the loss of 2,800 jobs.
Trees like maples, black walnuts, apples, and peaches suffer from heavy sap-sucking. High concentrations of the pests can suppress photosynthesis, stunt sapling growth, cause branch dieback, and stress mature trees.
Economists estimate that uncontained infestations could cost vulnerable agricultural states like Pennsylvania over $300 million annually in crop losses, nursery impacts, and management costs.

title: Couple bought 5 acres for $27,000; three cabins later made over $2.1 million
author: TOI WORLD DESK
text:
When Chris Broomfield, 51, a Connecticut carpenter, and his wife bought 5 acres of land in upstate New York, he already knew what he was going to do with the property. They bought the land in 2015 for $27,000. Eight years later, the rental cabins he built on that land had generated more than $2.1 million in revenue! Something that began as a weekend project to give his children a financial head start became a thriving hospitality business, a million-dollar business serving 
Airbnb
 guests across the region.
How a carpenter built a cabin empire
Chris Broomfield had spent decades doing carpentry contracting work. But there was a problem with passing that legacy forward. "Carpentry is a knowledge- and experience-based [business]," he told CNBC Make It. "I couldn't really hand that down to my kids. So I needed to build something that at least would give them a head start on something to borrow against or something that creates additional income." That's how it began.
In 2015, he bought a five-acre property in Remsen, New York. The land was close to the place where he grew up. His brother also had a property nearby. 
He saw potential in those rolling hills and the property's proximity to the lake. He thought multiple short-term rental cabins could bring visitors.
Broomfield began commuting eight hours every weekend from his Connecticut home to build an A-frame cabin largely by himself.
âI always knew it was going to be an Airbnb property. I knew I was going to put multiple cabins on it. I chose this property because it was close to the lake. It was very wooded, and it had rolling hills. I saw its potential with multiple cabins,â he said.
Three years into the process, he had completed a one-bedroom structure that would become his flagship property. The build cost roughly $90,000, though he hired outside help for specialised tasks such as drilling the well and handling electrical work. Broomfield's wife inspired a feature that guests couldn't stop photographing: a motorised king bed that slides out into the woods, letting renters sleep under the open sky. Along with it came a full kitchen, fireplace, fire pit and multiple decks. They listed the cabin for $60 a night on Airbnb. When demand spiked, the price went up to between $380 and $700 a night. By 2024, the A-frame was pulling in $119,337 annually, with 2025 projections near $143,500.
âThe process was amazing for me. I loved being up here. I loved being able to build anything that I wanted to build. Something that came from my mind and not a blueprint. The free rein was really enjoyable,â Broomfield told the publication.
More cabins
Once the A-frame cabin went viral, Broomfield moved quickly into his next project: a treehouse cabin. This time, he hired a team rather than doing it alone. Thirteen weeks later, in November 2019, the treehouse was finished. The treehouse, sitting 14 feet up, quickly grabbed attention. Guests had to cross a suspension bridge to reach it. Two bedrooms, a private pond with a dock, a covered porch and a living room overlooking a waterfall attracted families. In 2024, it generated $151,966 in revenue and ranked in Airbnb's top 10% by ratings and reviews.
Broomfield knew this was his true calling. He started building more. In 2021, he completed the Birch Falls Spa Cabin, a studio featuring an 18-foot indoor waterfall, massage bed and soaker jet tub. The $160,000 structure brought in $120,227 that year.
The monthly operating costs for the three cabins are about $8,000 in payroll and staff costs. Property taxes add $18,000 annually. Utilities run $700 a month. Against those expenses, Broomfield now pulls in roughly $400,000 a year! By September 2025, the cabins had earned him $2.1 million since the first one was listed for rent in 2018.
Broomfield has no plans to stop. Two more cabins were built: Tiny house, and 2-story container cabin. âThereâs always going to be something that is going to be pushing me to do the next thing. I canât sit back and do nothing. My family is a huge part of my inspiration and my drive; eventually, they are going to be the ones owning this,â he told the outlet. What started as a head start for his kids now became a family business. âThe legacy of Evergreen is, I donât really have a plan for it [but] I do know that it is going to inspire and help people. My kids are going to be a part of that.â
Now, Broomfieldâs day-to-day consists of overseeing his staff, designing new cabins and developing future plans for Evergreen Cabins.
Since retiring, Broomfield says itâs important for him to keep busy and keep building for his family.

title: H1-B visa price hike extension: How this will impact Indian engineers, technicians
author: TOI TECH DESK
text:
US President Donald Trump has extended sweeping restrictions on the H-1B non-immigrant visa route for an additional twelve months, keeping a mandatory $100,000 fee in place for specific foreign professionals, including technology workforce, looking to enter America. According to an official proclamation issued by the White House, the curbs originally implemented in September 2025 will now run through September 21, 2027. Administration officials stated the extension was required because the market conditions and alleged system abuses that triggered the initial rules continue to persist.
Key details of the $100,000 rule
Under the directive, foreign specialty occupation workers covered by the order cannot cross into the US unless their employer petitions include, or are supplemented with, a steep $100,000 payment. The payment condition hits employees situated outside the US who attempt to travel into the country after September 21, 2026.
The Homeland Security Secretary retains discretionary authority to grant waivers for an individual worker, a corporate workforce, or an entire commercial sector. However, this applies solely if the employment is certified as vital to US national interests and presents no threat to domestic safety or welfare. 
The administration says that third-party staffing agencies and IT outsourcing providers have long manipulated the visa route to displace American personnel with cheaper offshore talent.
âAs explained in the 2025 Proclamation, the H-1B nonimmigrant visa program was created to bring temporary workers in high-skilled functions into the United States, but it has been exploited to replace, not supplement, American workers with lower-paid labor.  Certain employers, including information technology (IT) staffing and outsourcing firms, have abused the system to suppress wages and displace American workers, and this has both harmed the labor market for American workers while also making it difficult to attract and retain the most highly skilled temporary workers.  IT staffing and outsourcing firms were found to supply a large volume of entry-level temporary Hâ1B workers, generally at a much lower salary compared to fullâtime, traditional workers, and some of these firms later outsourced IT roles to cheap labor markets overseas.  This has led to a proliferation of lower-paid foreign labor flooding the American labor market and making it difficult for American workers and recent graduates, especially in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) fields, to find employment.â
Why Indian engineers and skilled workers face the heaviest Blow
The decision delivers a hard setback to Indian software developers, engineers and technical personnel eyeing careers in the US. Indian citizens represent the overwhelming majority of program beneficiaries, making them uniquely vulnerable to rising regulatory costs.
Official US government figures from USCIS FY2025 H-1B report earlier this year show that Indian candidates secured nearly 70% of all approved H-1B petitions. China placed second by a wide margin, accounting for only 12.1% of approvals.
Under the old system, companies paid just $995 per applicant, which included a $215 lottery entry fee and an employer petition charge of $780. The new annual requirement of $100,000 is a more than 10,000% increase in costs and will require corporate sponsors to rethink how they hire internationally.
The rule imposes a massive financial hurdle for overseas candidates, making it prohibitively costly for American companies to hire them. Industry analysts expect corporate sponsors to pull back on applications, likely triggering a sharp decline in overall visa grants.
While senior specialists possessing niche, highly technical backgrounds may still secure backing, junior talent and early-career software developers face dwindling prospects as employers reconsider the heavy upfront investment.
âThe restriction imposed pursuant to subsections (a) and (b) of this section shall not apply to any individual alien, all aliens working for a company, or all aliens working in an industry, if the Secretary of Homeland Security determines, in the Secretaryâs discretion, that the hiring of such aliens to be employed as H-1B specialty occupation workers is in the national interest and does not pose a threat to the security or welfare of the United States.â
Last year, tech giants issued urgent travel advisories, triggering panic among foreign workers currently on leave or visiting family abroad, forcing corporate human resources teams to step in to protect their existing personnel.
Major corporate employers, including 
Amazon
, Microsoft, and JPMorgan, circulated urgent notices advising H-1B workers to remain stateside or immediately fly back to the US before the updated pricing rules take effect at midnight Saturday, September 20 2025.

title: Meet Neha Thakur, 25, Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver
author: etimes.in
text:
Itâs not easy to switch careers! But a young girl from Himachal Pradesh left her air hostess training to become a truck driver. Meet 25-year-old Neha Thakur who chose a career path few would have expected. After graduating, she worked briefly in the aviation sector and today, she spends her days behind the wheel of a 16-tonne truck, travelling across India. Neha belongs from Khudla village in Sarkaghat, Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. She is widely known as Himachal Pradeshâs first woman truck driver. She covers her journeys in her own social-media videos and vlogs.
The childhood connection
Trucks were a part of Nehaâs childhood because her father, Rajesh Thakur, has been a truck driver for more than two decades. Neha used to travel with him a lot. In one of her Instagram vlogs, she said that her father used to drop her in the school on a truck and she was quite fascinated by the vehicle.
That fascination stayed with her even after she chose a very different path.
After graduation, Neha went to Chandigarh and trained as an air hostess. She worked there, but the COVID-19 pandemic happened. The aviation industry was badly hit so she returned to her hometown after losing her job. 
Instead of viewing that setback as the end of her career, she began looking again at something that had interested her since childhood, truck driving.
Truck driving as a profession
It was not an easy decision. Neha had to learn how to handle a heavy commercial vehicle, understand gears, clutch and brakes. She joined a driving school and obtained her Heavy Motor Vehicle licence in 2023, when she was 21. Her father played an important role in her success. He supported her decision and helped her practise with the family truck, despite the criticism and scepticism surrounding a young woman choosing truck driving as a career.
Neha Thakur (Instagram)
The early journeys were largely local. Gradually, however, Neha moved on to longer routes. Today, she drives a 16-tonne Tata truck and has been reported transporting construction material and farm produce across interstate routes. Some accounts say she covers hundreds of kilometres during her journeys.
A new challenge
Driving a truck through the hills is demanding for any driver. People were often surprised to see Neha behind the steering of a heavy truck. She has spoken about the criticism and doubts she encountered when she chose this profession. But the more she drove, the less she had to explain herself.
Long journeys also meant irregular meals, changing weather and nights spent away from home. Driving through narrow mountain roads, fog, rain and difficult terrain requires concentration and patience. Neha's own social-media content has increasingly shown these less visible aspects of a trucker's life.
When the driver's seat became a camera
Neha also started her travel vlogging journey with this. She would record her journeys and post them on social media, giving viewers a look inside a profession most people experience only from the outside. Her videos cover her daily routine, long-distance journeys and practical aspects of handling a heavy vehicle.
She in one of the videos tells that soon her audience grew and she started getting brand deals. Reports published in 2026 put her YouTube following at more than 4.5 lakh, while her Instagram following has been reported at over 8 lakh.
More than a truck story
Neha never intended to become an inspiration or symbol of anything. She simply returned to something she loved and enjoyed. Her story moved from a child's fascination with her father's truck, to an air-hostess course, to finally choosing to do what she loved, the steering wheel.
Perhaps the most important part of Neha's story is therefore not that she chose a profession traditionally associated with men. It is that she allowed herself to change direction.
For Neha Thakur, the road eventually led back to the place where the fascination had begun with a truck, a mountain road and the confidence to take the wheel herself.

title: Alaska’s largest recorded gold nugget, found in 1998, later sold for $750,000
author: TOI WORLD DESK
text:
One push of a bulldozer turned an ordinary day of placer mining into a discovery that would enter Alaska's mining history. In 1998, miner Barry Clay was moving dirt near Ruby when he uncovered a massive natural gold-and-quartz specimen weighing 294.1 troy ounces, or more than 20 pounds. The Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys recorded the find as the largest gold nugget mined in Alaska. For more than two decades, the specimen remained a remarkable piece of mining history before Heritage Auctions offered it for sale in 2021. The nugget ultimately sold for $750,000, adding another extraordinary chapter to its story.
A discovery made while moving dirt
Clay was carrying out placer mining near Swift Creek, in the Ruby Mining District of Alaska's Yukon-Koyukuk Census Area, when the discovery occurred. According to Heritage Auctions' description of the specimen, Clay was using a bulldozer to push dirt when he noticed something unusual in the material he had excavated. Rather than leaving it behind with the surrounding material, Clay collected the object and took it into town for examination. It was subsequently identified as an exceptionally large gold nugget, making the find significant not only for its size but also for its connection to Alaska's long history of placer mining.
The nugget was later named the Alaska Centennial Nugget because it was found in 1998, a century after the Klondike Gold Rush era that helped make the region synonymous with gold prospecting. The specimen weighs 294.10 troy ounces, equivalent to about 9.14 kilograms, or just over 20 pounds. Its dimensions are approximately 17 by 14.5 by 11 centimetres. Rather than being a clean mass of pure gold, it is a natural gold-and-quartz specimen, with gold covering parts of a contrasting white quartz matrix.
More than just its weight
The size of the nugget is what immediately distinguishes it, but its appearance also contributed to its value as a collectible specimen. The auction house described the surface as having a complex, naturally formed structure, with visible gold running across the quartz-rich rock. Heritage Auctions classified it as a museum-quality specimen and highlighted its rarity as a large, naturally occurring gold specimen that had remained largely in its original condition.
An X-ray fluorescence, or XRF, analysis was also carried out on the gold visible on the specimen's exterior. The auction house reported an average surface purity of 87.59%, corresponding approximately to 21-karat gold. However, the specimen was not subjected to a conventional assay to establish its total gold content. Its owner considered the nugget's historical and collector significance more important than determining the exact amount of gold contained within it. This distinction matters because the 294.1-troy-ounce figure refers to the weight of the entire specimen, rather than 294.1 ounces of pure gold. The nugget contains quartz and other material alongside the visible gold.
From Alaska mining find to auction highlight
After its discovery, the Alaska Centennial Nugget entered a private collection. It remained there for years before being offered at Heritage Auctions' Nature & Science Signature Auction in December 2021. The auction took place on December 8, with the nugget becoming the headline lot. The auction record shows that the specimen sold for $750,000, with an internet bidder placing the winning bid. The sale made the nugget the highest-selling item in that auction, which generated more than $2.35 million in total sales.
The auction also demonstrated that the specimen's value extended well beyond the market price of its gold content. Large natural nuggets are unusual, and specimens that combine exceptional size, documented provenance and distinctive appearance can appeal to mineral collectors and museums. Heritage described the Alaska Centennial Nugget as the largest gold nugget ever found in Alaska and among the largest discovered in the Western Hemisphere. The auction house also noted that the Ruby Mining District has a history of producing large gold nuggets.
A record preserved in Alaska's mining history
The discovery is notable because it connects an individual moment of placer mining with a much broader chapter of Alaska's gold-mining history. Clay was not searching for a museum specimen when he began moving earth near Ruby; the extraordinary object emerged from ordinary mining activity. The Alaska Centennial Nugget subsequently became a documented record specimen. The DGGS publication identifies the 294.10-troy-ounce discovery as the largest recorded nugget mined in Alaska, while Heritage's 2021 auction record shows how that historic piece later moved from a private collection into the world of high-value mineral collecting.
More than two decades after Clay's bulldozer uncovered the unusual object, the nugget's journey reached another milestone. On December 8, 2021, the 20-pound-plus natural gold-and-quartz specimen sold for $750,000, turning a remarkable find from an Alaska mining claim into one of the most valuable mineral specimens offered at that auction.

title: Carrot Top hospitalized in Las Vegas; rep says comedian is recovering
author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
text:
Trigger warning: This story discusses suicide and a suicide attempt.
Comedian and longtime Las Vegas performer Carrot Top, whose real name is 
Scott Thompson
, has been hospitalized in Las Vegas following what TMZ reported as a suicide attempt. The 61-year-old comedian was reportedly rushed to a local hospital on Friday, September 18, after the incident, resulting in the cancellation of his scheduled Friday night performance at the Luxor.
Carrot Topâs representative, Jami Schlicher, confirmed that Thompson is recovering in hospital and receiving care and support.
âMr. Thompson is recovering in the hospital and is receiving the care and support he needs. His family and those closest to him are deeply grateful for the concern, prayers and respectfully ask for privacy,â Schlicher told TMZ.
No further details about Thompsonâs medical condition have been publicly released by his representative.
TMZ subsequently reported that police were seen at Thompsonâs Las Vegas residence following his hospitalization. The report said three police vehicles were photographed outside the comedianâs home on Friday afternoon.
Luxor show canceled following hospitalization
Thompsonâs scheduled September 18 performance at the Luxor was canceled following his hospitalization. The comedian has been a longtime headliner at the Las Vegas venue, where his prop-heavy comedy show has become a fixture of the Strip.
Carrot Top is widely known for his distinctive red hair, elaborate props and fast-paced stage performances. He rose to prominence in the 1990s through appearances on shows including Comic Strip Live and Star Search, before gaining wider attention following his 1992 appearance on The Tonight Show with Jay Leno.
He began his long-running Luxor residency in 2005 and has performed hundreds of shows a year during his Las Vegas run.
The hospitalization has also prompted renewed attention to Thompsonâs recent social-media activity, with fans leaving messages of support for the performer.
Note: If you or someone you know is struggling with suicidal thoughts or is in crisis, help is available. In the US, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. If there is an immediate danger, contact local emergency services or go to the nearest emergency department.

title: LPG Aadhaar rule from Oct 1: Authentication mandatory for these refills
author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
text:
LPG refill Aadhaar authentication rule: Domestic LPG consumers who have not yet completed their Biometric Aadhaar Authentication (BAA) will have to complete the process to book subsidised cylinder refills at regulated prices from October 1, 2026.
The Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry has said no further action will be required from the 27.43 crore consumers who have already completed the Aadhaar authentication.
As of September 19, biometric authentication had been completed by 89.9% of active domestic LPG consumers.
What happens if you donât complete Aadhaar authentication for LPG
Consumers who have not undergone BAA will not be stopped from receiving LPG cylinders. However, those who choose not to complete the authentication will have to pay the prevailing market price and will not receive the subsidy.
According to the government, the authentication requirement is intended to ensure that subsidised LPG benefits reach eligible households and to curb the diversion of domestic LPG cylinders for commercial and industrial use.
How consumers can complete authentication
Consumers have several options to complete Biometric Aadhaar Authentication. They can do it at the time of cylinder delivery, visit their LPG distributor's showroom, or use the mobile application provided by their oil marketing company.
Indane customers can complete the process through IndianOil ONE, while Bharatgas customers can use HelloBPCL. HP Gas consumers can authenticate through the HP PAY app.
Consumers who do not want to complete the authentication will have to record their choice through the digital channels of their respective oil marketing companies. They can still receive cylinders, but these will be supplied at market prices and will depend on local availability, according to an ET report.
Subsidy and compensation
Domestic LPG is sold at a price below its cost. The implicit subsidy on a 14.2-kg cylinder is estimated at around Rs 210 for September 2026, down from Rs 721 in June.
The government said it provided Rs 22,000 crore in compensation to oil marketing companies in FY23. It is paying Rs 30,000 crore in compensation in FY26 and FY27. As of August 31, 2026, the companies' accumulated under-recoveries from domestic LPG had crossed Rs 62,000 crore.
Consumers seeking help with LPG-related services can contact the toll-free helpline at 1800 2333 555.
PNG push
Meanwhile, despite the government's push to encourage a shift to cleaner piped gas, only around 20% of LPG consumers who have a PNG network in their neighbourhood and are eligible to make the switch have actually converted to PNG. The push followed the military conflict in West Asia earlier this year.
According to government data, city gas distribution (CGD) companies had identified 21.7 lakh consumers who had access to a PNG network and were eligible to switch. Of these, only 4.4 lakh consumers have applied so far, while PNG connections have been activated for 3.3 lakh consumers.
The identified consumers are located across more than 72,000 housing societies in 311 geographical areas. These areas have PNG networks operated by oil companies as well as public sector and private CGD entities.
Government data showed that more than 21 lakh households were contacted through WhatsApp messages, while eight lakh households received physical notices urging them to shift to PNG. More than 33,000 camps were also conducted as part of the exercise. Despite these efforts, the conversion rate remained low. Over the past five months, just over 1.4 lakh households have surrendered their LPG connections.
The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board had earlier launched two campaigns to encourage the adoption of PNG. However, the government's efforts intensified during the peak of the West Asia conflict in March and April, when disruptions to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz put pressure on India's LPG imports.
India consumed 33 million tonnes of LPG in 2025-26. Domestic production accounted for about 13 MT, while imports met the remaining requirement, with most of these supplies coming from West Asia. In contrast, the country is relatively more comfortable in terms of LNG supplies and domestic gas production.

title: Drake Maye studied Aaron Rodgers on YouTube, now he’s the NFL’s next star
author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
text:
When Drake Maye was nine years old, he watched 
Aaron Rodgers
 dismantle the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XLV. That game didn't just stick with him. It shaped him. Maye started studying Rodgers obsessively, right down to his throwing motion and pregame warmup routine. Fast forward to 2025, and the same kid is now an NFL starter, getting compared to Rodgers by opposing coaches, while Rodgers himself is winding down what could be his final season at 41.
How did Drake Maye become so obsessed with Aaron Rodgers growing up?
It wasn't just casual admiration. Maye carried an Aaron Rodgers phone case for years. He would pull up warmup clips on YouTube trying to decode how Rodgers gripped the ball and released it. "Shoot, it's hard to emulate the way he spins it. I mean, he spins it with the best of 'em," Maye said recently. That kind of fixation from a young quarterback is unusual. Most kids pick a favorite player. Maye picked a blueprint.
The Patriots selected Maye with the third overall pick in the 2024 draft, and from the moment he arrived in New England, the Rodgers comparisons followed him. He even got his boyhood moment when the Patriots faced the Jets in Week 3 of 2024. After the game, Maye lingered on the field, waiting. 
"I'm waiting for the GOAT," he told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo. He finally approached Rodgers, shook his hand, and said, "Big fan. Best of luck." Rodgers kept whatever he said next to himself. A private conversation, he noted.
That moment felt symbolic. The veteran acknowledging the kid quietly. The kid still starstruck but clearly ready.
Is Drake Maye already playing like Aaron Rodgers in the NFL?
The numbers in his second season suggest something real is developing. Maye has thrown for 1,744 yards with 12 touchdowns and just two interceptions, ranking sixth in the league in passing yards. An anonymous NFL coach watching him carved up the Titans told The Athletic's Mike Sando that a deep ball Maye threw to Mack Hollins on a 93-yard scoring drive was flat-out "Rodgers-like." That's not a throwaway comparison. That's a defensive coach, watching tape, reaching for one specific name.
Rodgers, meanwhile, just beat the Patriots in Week 3 of the 2025 season, 21-14, throwing the game-winning touchdown with two minutes left. He had the last word that day. But Maye, who finished with a 102.1 passer rating in that loss, isn't far behind. The gap is closing faster than anyone expected.
What makes this storyline different from the usual passing-of-the-torch narrative is that Maye didn't just idolize Rodgers from a distance. He studied him the way a student studies a subject. Every warmup rep. Every release point. Now those lessons are showing up on actual NFL Sundays, against actual NFL defenses.
Rodgers threw his first NFL touchdown pass in 2005. Drake Maye was barely five years old.

title: Daniel Bryan and Brie Bella’s marriage, family life and wrestling journey
author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
text:
Daniel Bryan, whose real name outside of WWE is Bryan Danielson, and Brie Bella, now Brie Garcia, have developed a relationship that has remained closely tied to professional wrestling, and the pair, who met while working in the WWE, tied the knot in 2014 and have continued to grow their family while juggling demanding careers in the wrestling industry.
In 2026, Brieâs WWE return puts their relationship back in the spotlight once again. Bryan has chosen a different path professionally, staying involved in wrestling but not on the same full-time basis as his former career. Today, their story is about balancing family responsibilities with two burgeoning professional paths.
Daniel Bryan and Brie Bella relationship in 2026
Daniel Bryan and Brie Bellaâs relationship blossomed during their time in WWE, where both of them became household names to wrestling fans; their romance eventually outgrew the wrestling world, and the two were married on April 11, 2014.
More than 10 years after they tied the knot, the couple still celebrate family and professional milestones together. Their relationship has withstood major evolutions in both careers, with Bryan stepping away from regular WWE competition and Brie taking time off from the ring.
The couple also share two kids, daughter Birdie Joe and son Buddy Dessert. Both have adjusted their professional schedules to allow for family commitments, and parenthood has become a major part of their lives.
Daniel Bryan and Brie Bellaâs family life
Daniel Bryan and Brie Bella are still most focused on their family in 2026. Raising two children and remaining connected to professional wrestling has meant both have had to navigate a schedule that can involve travel, appearances and long stretches away from home.
Brie scaled back her wrestling commitments as family priorities grew, and Bryan also had some major changes in his career. Both have been professional wrestlers, so they understand what it takes physically and professionally to get back in the ring.
The couple has kept their children out of the spotlight for the most part, but has given fans glimpses of family life now and then. Their method has allowed them to continue their wrestling careers as part of their public personas without making their family lives entirely public.
Brie Bella returns to WWE in 2026
Brie Bellaâs WWE return has been one of the biggest storylines surrounding her professional life in 2026. Her return to the ring brings her back to the company where she and her sister Nikki Bella became famous.
The Bella Twins became an integral part of the womenâs division in WWE, with Brie and Nikki becoming familiar faces inside and outside the ring. Brieâs latest return is merely another chapter in a career that has had plenty of breaks from wrestling.
Her return has also sparked a new interest in the couple due to Bryan Danielsonâs own extensive WWE history. So the pair remain connected to wrestling professionally, even as they move in different career directions.
Daniel Bryan supports Brie Bellaâs career
Now that Brie is back in WWE, Daniel Bryan's career has taken a different path. Bryan Danielsonâs professional wrestling journey continues as he moves away from the regular full-time schedule associated with his earlier WWE career.
That difference has opened up a new dynamic for the couple. But Brie can focus on her WWE commitments while Bryan is able to get involved in wrestling and family life in a different capacity.
Their 2026 relationship is more than their shared wrestling background. Marriage, parenthood and changing professional priorities have all become integral parts of their story, with Brie again in the WWE spotlight and Bryan on his own path, the couple remains linked by a long history in wrestling and a family life built outside the ring.

title: Yashasvi Solanki becomes first woman officer to serve as President’s ADC
author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
text:
In May 2025, Lieutenant Commander Yashasvi Solanki created history by becoming the first woman officer from any of India's three armed forces, the Army, Navy, or Air Force, to be appointed Aide-de-Camp (ADC) to the President of India. The President is traditionally assisted by five ADCs at any given time, three from the Army and one each from the Navy and the Air Force, a role that has for decades gone almost entirely to men. Solanki was formally presented with the prestigious aiguillette on May 9, 2025, officially marking her appointment for a tenure expected to last between two and a half to three years. Speaking about the unexpected nature of the opportunity, she has said in interviews that becoming the President's ADC was never something she had specifically dreamed of or planned for, largely because it hadn't seemed within reach. Her appointment came after a rigorous selection process, including an interaction with President 
Droupadi Murmu
 herself and the necessary security clearances, followed by a period of orientation before she formally took up her duties.
From district-level sports to the Naval Armament Division
13 Jul 2026 | 13:11
What's one stereotype about women that you're tired of hearing?
Solanki hails from Haryana, where her early life was shaped by fairly ordinary, disciplined surroundings. Before her defence career, she was known for her sporting ability, competing at the district level in both badminton and volleyball, activities that reportedly helped build the same discipline and focus she would later carry into her military service. She joined the 
Indian Navy
 in 2012 through the Short Service Commission, entering the Logistics Branch. 
Over the years that followed, she built a steady, well-regarded service record, eventually rising to become a technical officer in the Naval Armament Division based in Hyderabad. Officers selected for the President's ADC role typically bring at least five to seven years of strong, consistent service behind them, and Solanki's journey through logistics and technical postings gave her exactly that kind of grounded, hands-on experience within the Navy before this historic appointment.
What the role actually involves
As ADC, Solanki is now responsible for closely coordinating the President's official engagements, staying briefed on visiting dignitaries and upcoming events, and accompanying the President during state functions, investiture ceremonies, and diplomatic meetings. She has spoken about the level of preparation the role demands, noting that she and her colleagues must stay updated on who is meeting the President ahead of every engagement, since the President can ask about any of it at short notice. Her appointment reflects a broader, gradual shift already underway within the 
Indian Armed Forces
, including the Navy's evolving policies around allowing women to command warships and take on more cross-service responsibilities. It is worth noting that Solanki's milestone did not remain unmatched for long. In July 2026, Major Navya Shekhawat of the Army Service Corps became the second woman officer overall and the first from the Indian Army to be appointed ADC to the President, an appointment that built directly on the path Solanki had opened up a little over a year earlier.
A milestone that continues to inspire
Solanki's rise from a district-level sportsperson in Haryana to standing beside the President of India at Rashtrapati Bhavan is more than a personal career milestone; it reflects a slow but real shift in how India's armed forces are opening up their most prestigious ceremonial and protocol roles to women. For young women considering a future in the defence forces, her journey offers a clear, tangible example that roles once considered firmly out of reach are steadily becoming achievable through consistent, disciplined service.

title: How Vande Bharat Express marked a tech leap for railways. Next stop: Bullet trains
author: SMRITI JAIN
text:
In March 1969, 
Indian Railways
 flagged off its first Rajdhani Express train. In many ways the launch of Rajdhani Express trains heralded a new era for the national transporter - a fully air-conditioned train that technically broke the âspeed barrierâ for Indian Railways.
Almost two decades after that came the Shatabdi Express trains - a comfortable, day time travel experience that changed inter-city travel experience, taking it to a new level.
Fifty years after the first Rajdhani Express was launched, and over 30 years after the Shatabdi, came the Vande Bharat Express - a technological leap that has changed modern day travel on Indian Railways.
As Jagannarayan Padmanabhan, Senior Director and Global Head-Consulting, Crisil Intelligence says, Indian Railwaysâ passenger journey can be seen as a progression through three important generations of trains.
âRajdhani represented a fundamental shift towards faster, long-distance inter-city travel with a focus on connecting the national capital with major cities. Shatabdi took this further by making daytime inter-city travel faster and more convenient, particularly on shorter and medium-distance routes.â
âVande Bharat represents the next significant evolution, not simply because it is faster, but because it brings together speed, acceleration, passenger comfort, modern interiors, improved onboard services and a more contemporary travel experience,â he tells TOI.
In some ways, the story of India's premium passenger trains is a story of Indian Railways repeatedly pushing the limits of speed, comfort and technology. It is also the story of moving from ICF design coaches to LHB and now train sets with an aim to run trains that meet global standards.
The first Rajdhani and Shatabdi Express trains
Indian Railways has called the introduction of the first Rajdhani Express service a landmark moment. With its launch, India Railways broke a speed ceiling that had constrained Indian Railways for about a century.
The maximum operating speed on broad-gauge routes had at that time been limited to 96 kmph, and RDSO began a systematic study in 1960 to find ways of increasing speeds.
The breakthrough came after RDSO's recommendations were accepted by the Railway Board in June 1968, which concluded that speeds on the Delhi-Howrah route could be raised without large-scale capital investment in tracks, bridges or signalling.
Test and prototype rakes were run over the entire Delhi-Howrah route once a month for eight months, with trials conducted at speeds up to 136 kmph.
The journey of Rajdhani Express
The first Rajdhani then began service in 1969, running between New Delhi and Howrah at 120 kmph, covering 1,445 km in about 17 hours 20 minutes with three stoppages.
Sudhanshu Mani, retired ICF GM and the architect of the Vande Bharat Express trains calls the introduction of the Rajdhani Express as a watershed moment.
âThe track technology was improved so that trains could run at speeds of 130 kmph, and in fact because of that the tracks on which these trains were run started being called a Rajdhani-standard track,â he tells TOI.
âThe concept itself was related to overnight service with all needs taken care of, linen provided. What is also important to note is that at that time very few countries in Asia had trains that could run at speeds of 130 kmph, except for Japan. It was a turning point in terms of fast passenger service,â he explains.
The first Shatabdi was introduced in 1988 and was fully air-conditioned and fully reserved, with speeds reaching the 140 kmph mark. It became one of Indian Railways' fastest passenger services, building on the speed and premium-travel model established by Rajdhani.
Sudhanshu Mani notes that the new chair car design became a huge success.
G Raghuram, Advisor, The Infravision Foundation points out that Rajdhani and Shatabdi Express trains gave relatively faster travel options than Mail/Express trains and the brand name allowed for higher attention to be paid to service standards.
