Which is not to say that between Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Vande Bharat Express trains no upgrade in passenger travel took place. From Sampark Kranti and Duronto to Tejas and Humsafar Express - newer train concepts with better passenger amenities repeatedly took the spotlight.
âThere were other branded trains that were subsequently introduced - Sampark Kranti Express for example, connected one state to the other, with fewer stops in between, and more stops once the train reached the destination state. Duronto Express was launched with fewer stops and premium experience,â he says.
The coach technology also evolved. From using ICF design coaches to begin with, Indian Railways adopted the German technology Linke-Hofmann-Busch (LHB) coaches in 2003, with the first set used for Delhi-Mumbai Rajdhani.
G Raghuram, Advisor, The Infravision Foundation says ICF coaches were an improvement over existing railway coaches because they were non-telescopic - which meant that in case of a train crash, the coaches did not squash into each other. Then came LHB coaches with anti-climbing features, so that a crash did not cause coaches to climb on top of each other.
Indian Railways eventually stopped production of ICF design coaches, and now makes either LHB coaches or train sets.
Vande Bharat Express
Several years after the Rajdhanis and Shatabdis, in 2019 Vande Bharat Express marked the next big milestone for Indian Railways with several firsts. The 16-coach all air-conditioned train set ushered a new era of modern train travel in India.
Sudhanshu Mani, the ICF GM at that time spearheaded the project, and the train, called Train 18 at the time for its year of manufacturing (2018), was designed and rolled out in a record 18 months.
It marked Indiaâs entry into a semi-high speed self-propelled train set category - a train that could run at speeds of 180 kmph with no locomotive needed to pull it.
âVande Bharat is a train set and it matches a trend world over where trains are mostly run without a locomotive. Vande Bharat brought in a new technology for Indian Railways - a train set that could run at 180 kmph, upgradable to 200 kmph,â Sudhanshu Mani tells TOI.
Vande Bharat Express Key Features
And, the change is not limited to running trains faster. It has several important upgrades and features in terms of propulsion, braking, safety, passenger information and onboard systems.
The new train was swanky with a bullet train style conical nose and several aircraft style features.
One of the key engineering changes is the train's ability to accelerate and decelerate faster. This allows Vande Bharat to reduce journey times by up to 45% on several corridors.
The train boasts of European-style seats, automatic doors, GPS-based passenger information systems, onboard infotainment and regenerative braking, which helps improve energy efficiency during operations.
The train's mechanical design also focuses on improving the ride itself. Semi-permanent jerk-free couplers and improved suspension systems contribute to smoother travel, while regenerative braking allows energy efficiency to be built into the train's operation.
Centrally controlled automatic plug doors and fully sealed wider gangways further integrate the coaches into a single trainset rather than treating them as separate units.
Safety is another major technological component. Vande Bharat incorporates provision for KAVACH, India's indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection system, which is certified to Safety Integrity Level-4.
Vande Bharat Express Timeline
The train has constantly been upgraded and Vande Bharat 3.0 can now accelerate from 0 to 100 kmph in about 52 seconds, while also offering lower noise and vibration levels.
Another important leap is that the train sets and its systems are manufactured with around 90% localisation.
G Raghuram says that in terms of technology, Vande Bharat Express is the third big leap post independence in passenger train operations: from ICF design coaches to LHB coaches, and now a distributed power self-propelled train set.
âVande Bharat Express improves more on the crashworthy features,â he tells TOI. He says that the biggest USP of Vande Bharat Express trains is the fact that they are powered by linear induction motors.
âThe power is distributed which makes acceleration and deceleration quicker. This enhances the average speed of the train,â he says.
âAdditionally, the distributed power makes the ride jerk-free. In locomotive-powered trains such as Rajdhani and Shatabdi Express, even with modern technology and semi-permanent couplers, because the power of the train comes from the locomotive, there is a transmission lag, which results in jerkier rides,â he adds.
Vande Bharat sleeper
In 2026, almost seven years after the launch of the first Vande Bharat Express train, its sleeper variant was launched. Two prototype rakes run between Howrah and Guwahati, and many more are either being tested or are in the manufacturing stage.
While Vande Bharat addressed day time travel needs, the sleeper variant aims to revolutionise overnight travel. Apart from the benefits of the train set technology, Vande Bharat sleeper trains have passenger amenities and safety features that are superior to Rajdhani Express trains.
Vande Bharat sleeper: Key Features of the train
Around 260 Vande Bharat Express trains are expected to be rolled out in the coming years, covering high density railway networks, with speeds of over 130 kmph, and possibly even 160 kmph as the network gets upgraded.
The first ten train sets are being made by BEML in collaboration with ICF. Another 120 train sets will be made by Kinet (an Indo-Russian JV), and 80 by a BHEL-Titagarh Wagons consortium. ICF itself has been tasked with making 50 Vande Bharat sleeper train sets, with more coaches and a full pantry for longer distance overnight journeys.
So, what next?
The way forward
Bullet trains. India is now looking to manufacture its own high-speed train set capable of speeds of 280 kmph. The indigenously designed and developed train set is currently being manufactured by BEML and is expected to be rolled out for trials in early 2027.
The bullet train will run on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor, Indiaâs first, a part of which is scheduled to open in August 2027. The Rs 866.87 crore contract is for making two prototype bullet trains.
After Vande Bharat Express trains, experts see this as the next big railway engineering leap for India.
Railway experts say Vande Bharat Express trains set global standards, and revolutionized travel on Indian Railways. With bullet trains, India now looks to enter a new club.

title: AI to create many new industries in 5 years: Tata Sons chairman Chandrasekaran
author: VENKADESAN S
text:
CHENNAI: It may be unnerving to read negative stories about job losses due to AI and so on, but new sectors are opening, 
Tata Sons
 chairman 
N Chandrasekaran
 said on Saturday.
âThe art of the possible is becoming clear every day with AI, and it is going to throw up so many things we have not imagined today. New industries will come up in the next five years, but we may have not even known their terminology yet. And India is in a very strong position. India's economic growth will be unparalleled in our own history and in any part of the world," Chandrasekaran said while speaking at the convocation of SAI University near Chennai.
Chandrasekaran said the world is full to its brim with possibilities, though it is rapidly changing, disruptive and is increasingly becoming AI-led. He urged the young generation to keep learning and use social media to their benefit. "Make sure you read, watch and listen to what you choose to," he said.
Chandrasekaran said pressure would be a constant in one's life ever since passing out of college and that youngsters should learn to enjoy it all through their life. "To feel the pressure is a privilege," he said, quoting tennis legend Billie Jean King.
âThe will to win means nothing without the will to prepare,â he said quoting Tanzanian marathon runner Juma Ikangaa. 
"It applies to both sports and life. It is all about the willingness to put in the effort to prepare, and not about winning. Understanding what it takes to win is crucial," he said.
Stating that he himself is a runner (running is a hobby he took up 18 years ago), he advised students to run for themselves with a clear target in mind. "Life is a marathon race, not a sprint. It is about becoming better by the day, not overtaking others. There will be ups and downs. Don't fear downs, and do not turn your confidence into arrogance. Enjoy the journey," he said.

title: Hackers aren’t just stealing data anymore, they’re stealing your AI access
author: SUBHADRA SRIVASTAVA
text:
It sounds absurd: someone breaks into your system, and instead of emptying your database, they start making you pay for their AI.
But that is increasingly the point.
A stolen AI credential can give an attacker more than access to a company. It can give them computing power that the company has already paid for.
Attackers are increasingly stealing API keys, login sessions and other credentials that provide access to AI services, using them to run their own workloads, resell the access or hide behind legitimate customer accounts. The target is no longer necessarily the data sitting inside an organisation. In some cases, it is the AI access itself.
Anthropicâs September 2026 threat report describes an emerging criminal economy built around stolen AI access. Attackers are harvesting credentials from code repositories, mobile applications, websites, Docker containers, chatbots and other places where companies accidentally expose them. Those credentials can then be resold, used in further attacks, or simply used to run AI workloads at the legitimate customerâs expense.
The economics are simple: one stolen key can deliver three things - loot, compute and cover.
- Loot - because stolen AI credentials can be resold.
- Compute - because someone else can foot the bill for the workload.
- Cover - because the activity can look like it is coming from a legitimate customer.
CrowdStrike's 2026 Threat Hunting Report has observed a similar shift. 
In one campaign, attackers abusing corporate AI access generated nearly 200,000 API requests in an initial two-minute flood, using the victim's AI resources rather than simply stealing information from the account.
A stolen AI key can give attackers more than access â it can give them computing power.
AI access is becoming something criminals can sell
An API key is a string of characters that works like a digital pass. It allows an application to use an online service without a person having to log in each time. When linked to an AI service, that key can allow software to send requests to an AI model.
A session token serves a similar purpose. It is a digital proof that a user has already logged in and can allow continued access to an account.
If criminals steal either, they may not need the victim's password. They may be able to use the existing access instead.
Anand Venkatraman, Partner, Deloitte India, said this represents a change in how stolen credentials are viewed.
âAPI keys and session tokens have emerged as a new class of high-value digital assets. Historically, stolen credentials were a means to access networks, applications, or data. Today, the credential itself is often the target.â
The reason is simple. A working AI credential can already have an economic value.
âA live API key linked to a funded enterprise AI account is a monetizable asset that can be resold or abused directly, much like cloud credentials became valuable commodities once cloud compute gained economic value,â Venkatraman said.
In other words, criminals do not necessarily need to steal what an AI service has generated. They can steal the ability to use the service in the first place.
Anthropic says one hacktivist campaign ran for an entire month using stolen API keys. In another case, suspected ShinyHunters affiliates stole AI keys during an intrusion and switched their own attack workloads onto those keys.
The theft is also becoming industrialised.
One criminal pipeline downloaded 1.8 million Android APKs, decompiled them and searched them for hardcoded secrets. A separate harvesting operation collected GitHub personal access tokens. The stolen credentials were then validated and fed into criminal operations.
Another group went after users themselves by pretending to sell cheap access to frontier AI models. Victims who installed what appeared to be AI software instead handed over credentials and authenticated session tokens. The stolen access was then sold onward to other AI resellers.
And the target is not limited to ordinary AI users.
From exposed keys to underground brokers, stolen AI access can pass through several hands.
Criminals can make the victim pay for their AI use
AI services are generally paid for based on usage. The more a customer uses a model, the more computing resources are consumed and, depending on the service, the larger the bill can become.
This creates an opportunity for attackers.
They can take a stolen credential and use the victim's account to run their own AI workloads. This is sometimes referred to as LLMJacking, where criminals hijack access to an AI model and use the victim's computing resources.
CrowdStrike said it observed financially motivated criminals abusing corporate large language model, or LLM, access for LLMJacking and cost harvesting. In one campaign, attackers sent nearly 200,000 API requests in an initial two-minute flood.
CrowdStrike describes cloud resource hijacking as the unauthorised use of a victim's computing resources after an account is compromised. The same approach can be used for cryptocurrency mining or AI workloads, with the victim effectively providing the computing power and paying the associated cost.
Venkatraman said the economics are similar to earlier forms of cybercrime.
âThe move from data theft to access theft reflects a natural evolution of cybercrime. Underground markets have progressed from selling VPN and RDP access to cloud credentials, and now AI platform access.â
The attraction is that a stolen AI account may already have a payment method, an established usage history and access to models that could otherwise be expensive to use.
A legitimate account can also provide cover
There is another advantage for criminals. Activity carried out using a legitimate customer's account can be harder to distinguish from normal usage.
âA stolen AI credential isn't just reusable, it's a paid-for gateway: the attacker inherits legitimate compute quota and model access under someone else's billing and identity, making the activity far harder to flag than a conventional stolen password,â said Saurabh Sharma, security researcher, Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT), Kaspersky.
Hackers are increasingly treating AI credentials as digital assets that can be harvested and resold.
Venkatraman identified three reasons stolen AI credentials are attractive: they can be resold, they provide access to paid computing resources and they allow criminals to operate through a legitimate customer's account.
This means an attacker does not always have to create a new account or find a way to pay for AI services. The victim's existing access can do that work.
Developers are leaving credentials in places criminals can search
The growing value of AI credentials is also changing what criminals look for when searching the internet.
Anthropic said attackers have been searching public code repositories, mobile applications, container images and websites for API keys and session tokens. In one case documented by the company, an attacker stole AI API keys from an enterprise software vendor and subsequently used one of those keys for secondary attacks against other organisations.
The problem often starts with something as straightforward as a developer accidentally leaving a key inside software code.
Venkatraman said common sources include âHardcoded keys committed to repositories and exposed through forks or misconfigured CI/CD pipelinesâ, credentials embedded inside mobile applications, secrets included in container images and tokens exposed through client-side JavaScript.
A container image is essentially a packaged version of software that can be moved between computers or cloud services. If a secret is accidentally included in that package, anyone who obtains it may also obtain the credential.
Kaspersky has seen similar activity in developer tools. Sharma cited the 2025 singularity incident, in which attackers stole a package-publishing token and used it to push malicious npm packages designed to steal secrets from Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Amazon Q CLI.
AI access is becoming a new target as attackers seek keys, accounts, compute and billing access.
CrowdStrike also found attackers targeting software development environments, package registries and container registries. It said npm accounted for 87% of malicious software registry threats in the first half of 2026.
AI is adding more links to the supply chain
The term AI supply chain can sound abstract, but the idea is relatively simple. Companies increasingly connect AI services to their software, customer support systems, internal databases and automated assistants. Each connection needs some form of permission or credential.
That creates more places where access can be exposed or stolen.
AI agents are making this network wider. An AI agent is software that can carry out tasks on behalf of a user, rather than simply responding to a question. Such agents can be connected to email, messaging, calendars, company databases and other services.
Sharma said this is creating more potential routes into an organisation.
âAbsolutely every new integration point is a new credential to protect. We've flagged that AI agents are frequently connected to email, messaging, task-management systems, knowledge bases and MCP servers, meaning a malicious instruction or a credential leak can now originate from virtually any source the agent processes automatically.â
For companies, that means protecting an AI system is no longer only about securing the model itself. The credentials that connect the model to other services can become targets too.
Venkatraman said this is particularly relevant for Indian enterprises because AI deployments can also create new compliance responsibilities.
âThis trend resembles the evolution from "shadow IT" to "shadow cloud" and now "shadow AI." For Indian enterprises, governance challenges are amplified by requirements such as RBI outsourcing guidelines, CERT-In incident reporting obligations, and the DPDP framework.â
He said organisations should treat AI credentials with the same level of care as other privileged access, including limiting what each credential can do, regularly replacing credentials, monitoring their use and including them in incident response plans.

title: Scottish gran bought £15 ticket, won £4 million mansion plus £250,000 cash
author: TOI WORLD DESK
text:
A 72-year-old grandmother from Scotland was left stunned after initially believing she had won a horse, only to discover that she had actually scooped a Â£4 million coastal mansion in Cornwall with a Â£15 Omaze entry.
Mary Dickson, from Castle Douglas in south-west Scotland, almost missed out on the life-changing prize after ignoring calls from unknown numbers. When Omaze eventually contacted her and took her to a reveal location, she was even more confused when the first thing she saw was a horse standing in a field.
âI said thanks but no thanks!â
Recalling the unusual moment, Mary was quoted as saying by SWNS, âThe first thing I saw when I turned the corner was a horse. I said thanks but no thanks! Then I realised Iâd actually won a house, not a horse, so I quickly said thank you very much!â
Mary had entered the Omaze draw as part of her subscription, paying just Â£15 for the chance to win the four-bedroom property near the fishing village of Coverack in Cornwall.
The grandmother said she nearly missed the call confirming her win because she had no mobile signal and generally does not answer calls from numbers she does not recognise.
âI ignored Omazeâs calls at first. But they texted me, so I checked them out online, they looked like the real deal, so I thought Iâd better call back. Thank goodness I did!â she said.
âAll the family came to see the reveal, I was gobsmacked when they told me it was the house.â
The family later headed to a pub to celebrate, although Mary opted for coffee rather than an alcoholic drink.
âAlthough Iâm looking forward to a glass of wine by my new pool,â she added.
Four-bedroom mansion comes mortgage-free
The Cornwall home comes mortgage-free with Â£250,000 cash. (Photo: SWNS)
Mary and her husband John, 76, will receive the property mortgage-free, with stamp duty and legal fees covered. The prize also includes Â£250,000 in cash and Â£200,000 worth of furnishings.
The couple, who have lived in a terrace house in Castle Douglas since 2000, say they are in no hurry to decide what they will ultimately do with their new home.
âWeâre going to keep it for a while and just enjoy it and we canât wait to host Christmas here with all the family,â Mary said.
The property boasts panoramic sea views and direct access to Porthbeer Cove. Designed around its coastal setting, the house features floor-to-ceiling windows and four double bedrooms, three of which have dressing rooms and en-suite bathrooms.
The first floor includes an open-plan kitchen, dining and living area, along with a study, conservatory, boot room and utility room.
Outside, the expansive grounds feature a heated swimming pool with a swim-up bar, sunken banquette seating and a fire pit. There is also an outdoor kitchen with a barbecue and pizza oven, landscaped gardens and a private driveway leading to a three-car garage.
Despite the property having stables, Mary has made it clear that the couple are not planning to add horse ownership to their list of new commitments.
âThere must be something in the water up hereâ
The stunning mansion features a heated outdoor swimming pool. (Photo: SWNS)
Mary began entering Omaze draws after a colleague won an Omaze house in the Lake District in 2023.
âWhen I saw that heâd won, it made me realise real people really do win these houses - I did wonder if heâd used up all the luck around here, but it mustâve rubbed off on me,â she said.
âThere must be something in the water up here.â
Mary said she texted her colleague after discovering her own win because he was âthe only person I knew who could possibly know how I was feelingâ.
The couple last visited Cornwall around 20 years ago, when they travelled along the coast and stayed in hotels. They never imagined their next visit would involve viewing their own multimillion-pound home.
âWe never imagined that when we next came back to Cornwall, it would be to see our very own Â£4million mansion. Itâs absolutely stunning, we just canât believe itâs all ours,â Mary said.
âOur house in Scotland could probably fit on the turning circle on our new driveway.â
She also joked about the journey south, referencing Scottish band The Proclaimers.
âFunnily enough, The Proclaimers popped up on the telly promoting their new album the morning we went to see the house for the first time - fitting really, as we gladly went 500 miles to arrive at this door!â
A win that will change the familyâs future
The couple plans to celebrate Christmas in their new Cornwall home. (Photo: SWNS)
John spent 27 years working as a draughtsman at a Motherwell steelworks before moving into an IT role with the fire and rescue service. He retired in 2011.
The couple have been together since 1996 and married in 2017. Mary has two daughters, one of whom has sadly passed away. They remain close to her late daughterâs two sons, aged 17 and 22.
Mary said the win would have a lasting impact on the entire family.
âThis win is fantastic for all our family, weâll enjoy it together for now, and owning such a valuable property is life-changing for all of us,â she said.
Cornwall property sits near Porthbeer Cove
The mansion is located on the Lizard Peninsula, on the eastern side of the Cornwall National Landscape. Porthbeer Cove, a sheltered sandy beach, is a short walk away along the South West Coast Path.
Falmouth, known for its harbourside restaurants and galleries, is around 30 minutes away, while Redruth is the nearest mainline railway station, offering direct services to London Paddington.
Mary won the property through an Omaze draw conducted in partnership with Wellbeing of Women. According to Omaze, the draw guaranteed Â£1 million for the charity, while the company also committed a further Â£3.5 million through a separate multi-year grant.
Matt Pohlson, founder and CEO of Omaze, said the company was âover the moonâ that Mary and John had won the Cornwall property while supporting Wellbeing of Women.
âOmaze offers people the chance to win incredible prizes, whilst also introducing charities to new audiences that they wouldnât normally reach - itâs a win-win for entrants and our charity partners,â he said.
The company said the Omaze community has raised more than Â£150 million for good causes across the UK.

title: Johnny Carson’s Malibu estate once asked $81.5m, finally sold for $40m
author: TOI WORLD DESK
text:
Johnny Carsonâs former Malibu estate has had a remarkable journey through the luxury property market, moving from a roughly $9.5 million purchase in the 1980s to an $81.5 million asking price decades later before eventually changing hands for $40 million. The figures and property history were reported by the Mansion Global, with property records cited in their coverage. The late âTonight Showâ host bought the Point Dume estate in 1984 for about $9.5 million, according to the Los Angeles Times. Carson owned the property for more than two decades and continued to live there until his death in 2005 at the age of 79. The Malibu property was built in 1978 by architect Ed Niles and sits on slightly more than four acres overlooking the Pacific.
At the heart of the compound is a 7,083-square-foot modern home featuring a copper-and-glass sunken fireplace, media room, wine cellar and an indoor arboretum beneath a 30-foot-high glass ceiling. The estate also includes extensive outdoor spaces, a swimming pool, waterfalls, a koi pond and a sunken tennis court.
From Carsonâs home to an $81.5 million listing
After Carsonâs death, the property passed to his widow, Alexis. In 2007, she sold the home and its adjacent parcels to fashion mogul and film producer Sidney Kimmel and his wife, Caroline. 
The Los Angeles Times reported the transaction at about $46 million, while later coverage cited property records putting the figure at $36.5 million, reflecting differences in how the multi-parcel deal was reported.
A decade later, the Kimmels put the compound on the market for a staggering $81.5 million. The listing price was nearly nine times what Carson had paid for the estate in 1984. The property offered considerably more than just the main residence. A separate guesthouse stood on the adjoining land, while the tennis area included a pavilion with additional facilities. Its oceanfront setting and connection to one of American televisionâs most recognizable hosts added to its celebrity appeal. But the $81.5 million asking price did not translate into a sale.
Price cut still could not secure a buyer
By August 2018, the asking price had been reduced to $65.2 million, an approximately 20% cut from the original listing price, the Los Angeles Times reported. Even at that lower figure, the estate remained on the market. The eventual sale came in June 2019, when the compound changed hands for $40 million. Mansion Global reported that the main house accounted for $25.9 million, while the two adjacent lots together sold for $14.1 million. That represented roughly a 51% reduction from the original $81.5 million asking price.
The deal was still above the price cited by Mansion Global for the Kimmelsâ 2007 acquisition, but it was far below the ambitious figure attached to the property when it first returned to the market in 2017. The buyerâs identity was not publicly established in the 2019 report, with Mansion Global noting that the property was acquired through a limited liability company. Later reporting identified venture capitalist Riaz Valani and his wife, Augusta Tigrett, as the buyers in an off-market transaction valued at $40 million.
The estateâs price history ultimately tells a striking story of Malibu luxury real estate: Carsonâs roughly $9.5 million purchase in 1984 became a $46 million-or-thereabouts transaction in 2007, an $81.5 million asking price in 2017 and, after a major reduction, a $40 million sale in 2019. The property has since returned to the market, with a $110 million asking price reported in 2025.

title: Telangana High Court awards one-month jail term to DSP in contempt case
text:
Justice K. Sujana of the Telangana High Court sentenced police officer A. Krishnaiah, who went on sick leave while serving as L.B. Nagar Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) of Malkajgiri commissionerate, to undergo one-month imprisonment, convicting him in a contempt of court case. The judge also imposed a fine of ₹2,000 on the officer.
The judge, however, suspended operation of the sentence till October 19 providing an opportunity to Krishnaiah to go for an appeal following the request of Public Prosecutor for Home Palle Nageshwar Rao. The contempt petition was filed by Katta Vamshi Krishna contending that Krishnaiah arrested him in a case of dowry death despite a specific order issued by the HC granting him protection from arrest.
The Bench of Justice K. Sujana on April 21 passed an order not to arrest the petitioner till April 23 and further extended the order on April 27. However, Krishnaiah, who was the investigating officer, arrested the petitioner on April 28 and produced him before the local court which rejected remand of the petitioner on learning that HC had passed protection from arrest order in the case.
“It was incumbent upon him to ascertain whether the said protection had been extended..”, the judge said. The officer cannot contend that he was unaware of the orders passed by the court, the judge said.

title: 51,000 appointment letters distributed at Rozgar Mela in the country: V. Somanna
text:
Union Minister for Railways and Jal Shakti V. Somanna said the Central government was implementing several schemes to provide young people with opportunities in skill development, employment and entrepreneurship, recognising their role in the country’s overall development.
He was speaking after inaugurating a Rozgar Mela at the auditorium of the All India Institute of Speech and Hearing (AIISH) in Mysuru on Saturday.
The Rozgar Mela, organised under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, saw appointment letters being distributed to more than 51,000 candidates across various parts of the country. The programme reflected the government’s priority towards creating employment opportunities for the youth, he said.
Mr. Somanna highlighted the Skill India Mission and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, launched in 2015, under which crores of young people had received skill training and certification. The number of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) had also increased significantly, providing greater access to vocational training, he said.
He said the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme had helped lakhs of young people gain training and practical work experience. The Pradhan Mantri Setu scheme, with an outlay of ₹60,000 crore, was aimed at modernising around 1,000 ITIs and providing modern technical training facilities, he added.
Emphasising the importance of entrepreneurship, the Minister said the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana was providing loans to small traders, hotel owners, transport operators and small entrepreneurs. A large number of beneficiaries in Karnataka had also received financial assistance under the scheme, he said.
Mr. Somanna urged the youth to view their employment not merely as a means of livelihood, but also as an opportunity to contribute to nation-building. He advised newly appointed employees, including those joining the Railways and other Central government departments, to uphold integrity and honesty in their service.
He also highlighted efforts to expand educational opportunities in medical, engineering and other higher education fields, along with investments in education, healthcare, skills and digital infrastructure.
Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar said appointment letters were being distributed to around 51,000 candidates as part of Rozgar Melas held across the country. He described the programme as an important platform for creating new opportunities for young people.
Mr. Wadiyar said India had witnessed changes in the economy, infrastructure, employment and public welfare sectors under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership since 2014. He also referred to India’s growing international presence, poverty reduction efforts and initiatives such as Swachh Bharat.
The country’s cultural heritage, including Mysuru’s yoga tradition, was also gaining global recognition, he said, calling for collective efforts towards national development.
AIISH Director Pushpavathi, CGST Commissioner Ravindra Radha, newly appointed candidates and officials were present.

title: IIT Bombay faculty member booked for caste abuse, suicide abetment
text:
The Mumbai Police on Saturday (September 19, 2026) booked IIT Bombay faculty member Suryanarayan Dulla, alleging caste abuse and abetment to suicide, a day after a 22-year-old student was found dead in his hostel room.
The student, Sahil Wakode, was pursuing his second year in BTech Energy Science. In a statement, IIT Bombay said he died by suicide after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone during an examination.
The police filed a first information report on Saturday (September 19, 2026) on a complaint from the student’s father, Chakradhar Wakode. Mr. Dulla, working in the Energy Science department, was booked under various sections of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, and on abetment to suicide charge.
“When Sahil was studying in the second year, when I met him, he said that for the last three months, on the instructions of Director Shri Shireesh B. Kedare, faculty member Suryanarayan Dulla had been abusing him using caste terms. Mr. Dulla told him that he was from a ‘lower caste and he [Mr. Dulla] can harass him and implicate him in any false case.’ After that, I gave him mental support,” Mr. Chakradhar said in the FIR.
Mr. Chakradhar mentioned “other senior officers” in addition to Mr. Dulla, in his complaint.
In its initial statement expressing condolences, IIT Bombay said Sahil had uploaded the third semester examination question paper on ChatGPT to seek answers. Going by the statement of a student who was also present in the same building during the examination, Mr. Dulla caught Sahil and allegedly threatened debarment. Mr. Dulla also told him to attend a meeting the next day regarding the incident, the student said. Sahil left the examination hall immediately and was later found dead in his room in hostel number 4 on the campus.
The student said that a high-stress environment prevailed in IIT Bombay, which is among the top technology institutes in India. “This is the second suicide in hostel four in recent months,” the student said in a telephonic conversation.
The students erupted in protest after the incident. The resignation of the IIT Bombay Director is one of their demands, said the student, who is among the protesters. The police are investigating the circumstances surrounding Sahil’s death.
(Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416. and Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050).

title: 21,000 unfinished 2BHKs in Hyderabad (CURE) completed; beneficiary selection by end of October
text:
The unfinished works at around 21,000 double bed room houses in Hyderabad (CURE) were completed. Housing Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy directed officials to complete the draw of lots to select beneficiaries by the end of the month (September).
The 21,000 double bedroom houses (2BHK) are located in 26 areas within the Core Urban Region (CURE). People living within five to seven kilometres of the houses should be selected, said Mr. Reddy at a video conference held with Collectors of Hyderabad, Rangareddy, Sangareddy and Medchal districts, and officials from Electricity, Water Works and Housing Departments on Saturday (September 19). He said that the works were left unfinished by the previous government.
They were directed to ensure basic resources, including water, electricity supply and sanitation, are provided by the end of October.
People who were earlier allotted the 2BHKs but not staying there may receive another notice as the Housing Minister issued instructions to this effect. If there is no response to a notice, the allotment should be canceled and another beneficiary has to be selected, he said.

title: II PU exam, marks card fee and others up by 50% from this academic year in Karnataka
text:
After almost eight years, the examination fee, admission fee for examination, marks card fee and others for II PU students in both government and private colleges across the State has been increased by 50%.
The government order stated that the Department of Pre-University Education and Karnataka State Examination and Assessment Board (KSEAB) had proposed to increase the exam and other related fees.
A KSEAB official said, “The exam fee hike was proposed two years ago and it was not increased for various reasons. The same fee has continued since 2018. Now that the paper and printing costs have increased, the fee had to go up too.”
With this hike, the fee for admission for exams has gone up from ₹400 to ₹ 600, the migration fee has increased from ₹480 to ₹720. Repeaters must pay ₹210 instead of ₹140 for one subject, ₹405 instead of ₹270 for two subjects, ₹600 instead of ₹400 for three subjects. Meanwhile, the exam fee for practical exams has increased from ₹ 110 to ₹165 for one subject.
For the first time, the department has included fee for II PU marks card verification for Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) and for foreign universities, which is ₹2,000.
Students are not pleased with the move. Karthik M, studying in the Government PU college in Rajajinagar, said, “My father and mother are flower vendors and this hike is going to burden us.
Likitha, a student at a private college in Vasanth Nagar, said, “My father is a private bus driver and my mother is a homemaker. Amidst financial constraints, they have admitted me to private college where my fee is ₹95,000 per year. Increasing exam fee, marks card fee by almost 50% is burden to my parents. As private college student, I cannot even oppose or request the administration to wait until I pay the fee.”
Meanwhile, there is demand to increase the evaluation fee from lecturers. A.H. Ningegowda, President, PU Lecturers Association, said, “The salary for evaluation depends on the number of papers evaluated. For one answer script evaluation, it is ₹36, which has remained the same for five years. Lecturers across the State have not received a single penny of the second round of exam paper evaluation of II PU exams conducted recently.”

title: Former V-P Ansari remembers ‘one-man institution’ A.G. Noorani
text:
Renowned columnist and legal expert A.G. Noorani was remembered at a memorial lecture at the India Islamic Cultural Centre in New Delhi on Friday (September 19, 2026), where former Vice-President M. Hamid Ansari described the former The Hindu and Frontline columnist as a “polymath” and “one-man institution”.
Calling Mr. Noorani as one of the sharpest minds on constitutional law, Mr. Ansari said he had his own distinctive way of working. Although he was not a grassroots reporter, Mr. Noorani understood the pulse of the nation, he said. The Noorani Records, a publication of The Hindu Group containing some of the best writings of the late columnist, was also released by Mr. Ansari in the presence of former Union Minister Salman Khurshid. Mr. Noorani wrote for The Hindu and Frontline for nearly four decades.
In his speech, titled ‘Remembering a Polymath: The Life and Times of Abdul Ghafoor Noorani’, Mr. Ansari said Mr. Noorani’s life and work reflected an unwavering commitment to justice, civil liberties, minority rights, secularism and constitutional governance.
Recalling various facets of Mr. Noorani’s personality, Mr. Ansari said he was well respected among lawyers in the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court. On issues ranging from constitutional amendments and the Anti-Defection Bill more than 30 years ago, to the more recent Citizenship (Amendment) Act, Mr. Noorani wrote with “rare perspicacity”, he said. He also wrote on the "troughs and crests” of Kashmir.
Born in erstwhile Bombay into the Kutchi Memon community, Mr. Noorani guarded his privacy and was not known to mingle easily with people. He spent his time reading and writing. After his death, his vast collection of books was sent to the Jharkhand High Court library, after a section of lawyers opposed the proposal to keep the books in the Bombay High Court.
“He was a polymath and much more,” Mr. Ansari said, adding, “His writings covered domestic politics, jurisprudence, international relations and history, often bringing together legal, political and historical perspectives.”
For a good part of his address, Mr. Ansari focused on Mr. Noorani’s contribution to the defence of human rights and constitutional freedoms. He described him as a fierce defender of civil liberties, minority rights and constitutional governance, particularly at a time when State power and legislation posed serious questions for individual freedoms.
Mr. Noorani’s writings repeatedly examined State overreach, secularism and religious equality. Mr. Ansari said his approach was rooted in the defence of fundamental freedoms and opposition to oppressive legislation and injustice.
Among Mr. Noorani’s early works was his 1963 biography of then President Dr. Zakir Husain. The book carried a foreword by Jayaprakash Narayan, who praised Husain’s “active, creative, refined, dedicated, fearless and truthful” life. Mr. Ansari also recalled that a reproduction of painter M.F. Husain’s portrait of Mr. Noorani appeared in the volume.
Mr. Noorani’s concern with justice was also reflected in The Trial of Bhagat Singh: Politics of Justice, in which he argued that Bhagat Singh and his colleague had been victims of a miscarriage of justice amounting to judicial murder.
His scholarship was not confined to Indian constitutional and political questions. His study of the India-China boundary dispute, covering from 1846to 1947, examined the historical origins of one of India’s major foreign-policy challenges. Mr. Ansari described his treatment of the dispute as a combination of history, law, morality and political expediency.
Among those present were former Union Ministers Salman Khurshid and Mani Shankar Aiyar, besides diplomats, bureaucrats and authors.
Published - September 19, 2026 09:47 pm IST

title: Hyderabad roads waterlogged, traffic hit as heavy rain coincides with Ganesh immersion rush
text:
Heavy rain lashed several parts of Hyderabad on Saturday evening after days of hot and humid weather, causing waterlogging and disrupting traffic at several locations across the city. The rain also compounded the weekend rush as large numbers of devotees visited Ganesh pandals, particularly in Khairatabad and Begum Bazaar.
The city, which witnessed bright and sunny conditions during the morning, turned cloudy after noon, with rainfall beginning in several areas after 4 p.m.
Waterlogging and slow-moving traffic were reported at Shaikpet flyover, Manikonda-Tolichowki towards Gachibowli, Iqbal Minar Road towards the Secretariat, NMDC towards Masab Tank, Banjara Hills Road No. 12 near Agrasen Statue towards Omega Hospital, Shivrampally, Rajendranagar, Aramghar RUB, BN Reddy Nagar towards Hasthinapur X Road, and Nagole towards Bandlaguda.
The rain further affected traffic movement in areas witnessing heavy footfall for Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations. With a large number of devotees visiting the Khairatabad Ganesh idol, congestion was reported in Lakdi-ka-pul, Somajiguda and surrounding areas.
Traffic movement was also slow around Begum Bazaar, where devotees were visiting the Ganesh pandal amid congestion on narrow roads. Vehicles moved slowly along Malakunta Road and Begum Bazaar Chatri towards MJ Bridge on both sides.
Traffic police personnel from Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Malkajgiri commissionerates along with Disaster Response Force (DRF) personnel from Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) were deployed at major junctions across the city to clear waterlogging and ensure smooth flow of traffic.
According to data from Telangana Development Planning Society (TGDPS), as of 9 p.m., Nagole recorded 63.3 mm rainfall followed by 59.5 mm in Shamshabad, 44.5 mm in Sivarampally, 44.5 mm in Rajendranagar, 40.8 mm in Attapur, 31.3 mm in Shaikpet, 29 mm in Adibatla, 28.8 mm in Bandlaguda, 24.3 mm in Vanasthalipuram, 23.5 mm in Hayathnagar and 20.5 mm in Khairatabad.
The rain also affected flight operations at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA), with two flights diverted. According to FlightRadar24, IndiGo flight 6E 6063 from Shirdi was diverted to Vijayawada, while IndiGo flight 6E 1182 from Colombo was diverted to Bengaluru.
Meanwhile, several parts of the city did not receive any rain and remained largely dry.

title: ABVP wins 3 DUSU posts; independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen gets vice-president’s position
text:
The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) on Saturday (September 19, 2026) bagged three Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) central panel posts, while an Independent candidate, earlier associated with National Students’ Union of India (NSUI), won the vice-presidential post.
Like last year, ABVP won the posts of president, secretary and joint secretary. However, this year saw a neck-and-neck battle with NSUI trailing in two posts. ABVP’s total winning margin came down from 23,873 last year to 9,671 this year. The voter turnout increased from 39.5% last year to 40.46% this year.
This year’s student elections took place against the backdrop of Jantar Mantar protests in the city, which saw many Delhi University students participating in it. The polls also happened in the wake of the paying guest building collapse in Satya Niketan area, which has led to student protests for better accommodation facilities.
ABVP’s Yash Dabbas won the president’s post upon receiving 24,576 votes while NSUI’s Vijay Shankar Meena came in second with 22,523 votes.
The vice-president’s post was bagged by Deepanshu Shokeen, an Independent candidate. With 30,615 votes, he won with the highest number of votes, and the widest margin of the four winners. Ishu Maurya from ABVP trailed him with 16,901 votes.
ABVP’s Riya Chhawdi was elected DUSU secretary with 21,650 votes, beating NSUI’s Namrata Chaudhary who finished with 14,869 votes. For the joint secretary post, Lakshay Raj Singh from ABVP won with a slim margin of 813 votes. Vishesh Yadav from Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha (SCS) came in second, while NSUI came in third.
President-elect Mr. Dabas said: “Delhi University’s Gen-Z has given a clear message that it believes in social harmony and nationalism. I will work to transform this trust into responsibility and ensure that the voice of every student is represented strongly through the students’ union.”
The organisation will focus on student safety, better facilities, equal opportunities and a positive academic environment, said Ms. Chhawdi, the Secretary-elect. “We will work to ensure that the concerns of students, particularly women students, receive due attention,” she added.
BJP congratulates ABVP
BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday extended his wishes to the ABVP’s victory in DUSU elections. “Congratulations to all my young friends at Delhi University on ABVP’s historic victory in the DUSU elections! This victory reflects the youth’s continued faith in positive and constructive student politics, rooted in the spirit of Nation First, and their strong resolve to contribute to the vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat’,” he said.
Last year, the presidential candidate from ABVP had won with a margin of 16,196 votes whereas this year it came down to 2,053. Similarly, the joint secretary post was secured by ABVP last year with a margin of 4,445 votes, as opposed to 837 votes this year. The margin for secretary’s post went up this year to 6,781 from 3,234 last year.
Visually-impaired candidate
Aam Aadmi Party’s student body Association of Students for Alternative Politics fielded a visually-impaired candidate for the first time in DUSU elections for the post of secretary. The candidate, Pankaj Kumar Dhingra, received 7,639 votes.
While the joint Left panel with All India Students’ Association (AISA) and Students’ Federation of India (SFI) had hoped to challenge the ABVP-NSUI binary, but their performance was similar to previous years.
While some students pointed out that the Left organisations were active during Jantar Mantar, this did not drastically change their vote share from previous years. Presidential candidate Ananya Raturi got 5,377 votes, coming in third. They came in third in the secretary’s election too, garnering 8,734 votes.
Like last year, many students also opted for the NOTA button. As many as 4,310 students pressed NOTA for president, 4,359 for vice-president, 7,884 for secretary and 7,389 for joint secretary.

title: Karnataka ranks third in NITI Aayog’s electric mobility index 2025
text:
Karnataka has emerged as one of India’s top-performing States in electric mobility, securing the third position nationally with a score of 73 in the India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) 2025 released by NITI Aayog on Saturday.
Karnataka is also among the two leading large States classified as top performers, alongside Maharashtra, reflecting its progress in advancing electric mobility.
Delhi topped the overall rankings with a score of 84, followed by Maharashtra with 78. Karnataka secured 73, followed by Chandigarh, 71, and Goa, 65. The Index classifies jurisdictions scoring 65 and above as top performers.
Charging facility
Karnataka recorded a score of 97 in Charging Infrastructure Readiness (CIR), the highest in the country, highlighting the State’s progress in developing the infrastructure required to support electric vehicle adoption.
In IEMI 2024, Karnataka ranked fourth in the country with a score of 64 and was listed in the top performers’ category after Delhi, Maharashtra, and Chandigarh.
This is the second edition of IEMI, developed by NITI Aayog in collaboration with WRI India. It evaluates the progress of States and Union Territories towards electric mobility, covering both policy frameworks and implementation outcomes.
Dedicated policy
Receiving the recognition at the launch of IEMI 2025 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, Additional Chief Secretary, Energy, Gaurav Gupta, said: “Karnataka’s electric mobility initiatives include Bescom EV Mithra, a unified electric vehicle charging app, a single-window clearance system and an EV Accelerator Cell. Karnataka was also the first State in India to introduce a dedicated electric vehicle policy in 2017, covering vehicle sales, charging infrastructure and dedicated manufacturing zones.”
Mr. Gupta added that Karnataka currently has 6,979 EV charging stations, including 4,896 in Bengaluru. “EV sales are also on the rise, with penetration close to 15% during the first five months of FY 2026–27. The State has recorded the third-highest cumulative EV sales in the country after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra,” he said.
Elaborating on the EV registrations, he said Karnataka accounts for 8.81% of India’s overall EV registrations. The State is second in both two-wheeler and four-wheeler registrations, after Maharashtra. In e-bus registrations, Karnataka ranks third, after Delhi and Maharashtra.
Meanwhile, K.J. George, Minister for Energy and Tourism, said that Karnataka will continue to strengthen its electric mobility ecosystem through supportive policies, infrastructure development and initiatives that facilitate wider adoption of electric vehicles.

title: Basavadi Sharanara Hindu Samavesha triggers debate among religious heads
text:
The proposed Basavadi Sharanara Hindu Samavesha, scheduled to be held in Kalaburagi city on September 27, has sparked a debate among religious heads and followers of Basava philosophy, with different groups of seers taking contrasting positions on the event and its nomenclature.
Koraneshwara Swami of Anubhava Mantap in Aland and Basava Prabhu Swami of Gunateerthawadi in Basava Kalyan addressed the presspersons on Saturday and opposed the proposed convention, alleging it sought to offer a different interpretation of the vachanas of the 12th-Century social reformer Basaveshwara and could confuse his followers.
Basava Prabhu Swami objected to including the word ‘Hindu’ in the convention’s title. He said the organisers should remove the word ‘Hindu’ and maintain the event strictly within the philosophical and social framework of the Sharana tradition.
Referring to the participation of Adrushya Kadasiddeshwar Swami of Kaneri Mutt in earlier programmes of a similar nature, Koraneshwar Swami said some of his remarks had offended those who followed Basaveshwara’s ideology. He maintained that the Basava philosophy should not be interpreted in a manner that diluted its fundamental principles.
They expressed their support for the protest being organised by the Basava Tatva Haagu Samvidhana Rakshana Horata Samiti in Kalaburagi on September 25 against the proposed convention. The protest is aimed at opposing the use of the word ‘Hindu’ in the name of the event.
However, another group of religious heads comprising Parmananda Swami of Aland and Chandragund Swami of Honnakiranagi defended the proposed convention and said there was no question of either distorting or misinterpreting Basaveshwara’s vachanas. They said nearly 300 religious heads from different Mutts were expected to participate in the September 27 gathering.
Parmananda Swami said Kadasiddeshwar Swami would primarily speak about agricultural practices and issues concerning farmers, to help them improve their knowledge and economic prospects. He said that although the Swami would refer to Basaveshwara’s vachanas, interpreting them in the contemporary context could not be equated with altering or distorting their meaning.
“Basaveshwara’s vachanas can be recited and discussed on any platform,” the seer said, questioning the basis for objections to their interpretation.
He also questioned the argument that the teachings of Basaveshwara should be separated from the broader Hindu tradition. “Were the Sharanas not Hindus?” he asked, arguing that the spiritual and philosophical legacy of the Sharanas could be discussed in a wider religious and social context.
Chandrakant Patil, organising president of the samavesha, said that official permission for the event is yet to be granted. He stated that preparatory meetings would be held across the taluks of the district to mobilise public participation and ensure the event’s success.

title: Study attempts to find out how India made expensive diabetes medicines affordable
text:
A study by Chennai-based diabetologists has attempted to find out how India has managed to reduce the prices of new and expensive diabetes drugs and what lessons this could possibly hold for other low- and middle-income countries (LMIC). The study, ‘Making Modern Diabetes Medications Affordable and Accessible: Lessons from India for Other Countries’, was led by V. Mohan, chairman, Dr. Mohan’s Diabetes Specialities Centre, Chennai, and was published in the journal Diabetes Care.
What did the study find?
Of the 589 million adults in the world with diabetes, 80% live in LMICs, the study noted. Modern diabetes therapies such as GLP-1 receptor agonists as well as SGLT2i (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors) improve cardiovascular and renal outcomes, while analogue insulins help reduce the risk of hypoglycaemia. However, affordability remains a barrier: diabetes requires lifelong care and management of complications.
India’s ability to maintain low medication prices is closely linked to its role as a major pharmaceutical exporter, the paper stated, noting the strategic legislative history of maintaining critical safeguards to prevent ‘patent evergreening’ and allowing for generic manufacture of drugs. It also found that the country has increasingly focused on strengthening domestic manufacturing capacity. There are concerns over global trade policies affecting prices and the availability of raw materials. A government incentive scheme has been introduced to promote domestic manufacturing of raw materials, and as of 2025, production has commenced for 26 molecules that were previously imported.
The paper notes that metformin and sulfonylureas continue to form the foundation of type 2 diabetes management in India - both are included in the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM). While DPP-4 (dipeptidyl peptidase 4) inhibitors, SGLT2i and GLP-1 RA have all been introduced, they are not currently in the NLEM. Initial uptake of these drugs was constrained by pricing. Following the competitive entry by multiple domestic manufacturers, the price of semaglutide, for instance in India, has dropped considerably now, and there has been a huge increase in sales; however, absolute monthly costs remain high relative to the household income in India, and, crucially, these are not covered by insurance, as they are, to a great extent, in the U.S.
Quick availability of generic and biosimilar drugs, deliberate regulatory and distribution strategies such as the government’s Jan Aushadi Kendras, and market competition have allowed for affordable drugs in India, the paper highlighted.
What does it propose for other LMICs?
Building local manufacturing capacity as a strategic public health investment, balancing patent governance that encourages easier access to newer molecules, predictable and structured price regulation, good distribution networks at reasonable retail prices and aligning pharmaceutical policy with health financing and ongoing monitoring of medicine quality, prices, prescription patterns and patient access can all help with improving access to affordable medicines, the paper noted. These core principles could also apply to high-income countries facing drug prices, the paper said.
Challenges ahead
Challenges that remain include urban-rural disparities in distribution and availability of medicines; tight regulations potentially affecting chances of drug innovation; differences in quality between generics and difficulties in maintaining strict pharmacovigilance; as well as limited formal evaluation of government schemes to look at their long-term impact on clinical outcomes.

title: After Sagar tragedy, Madhya Pradesh Police uncover hooch racket with Delhi link
text:
After at least 20 people died earlier this month in a hooch tragedy in Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar district, the police have uncovered a Statewide counterfeit liquor manufacturing cartel with links to Delhi, officials told The Hindu on Saturday (September 19, 2026).
According to officials, 14 people were arrested over the previous two days. Among them was the owner of a chemical company in Delhi, who is accused of supplying industrial spirit to those involved in manufacturing counterfeit liquor.
Investigating the first two information reports (FIRs) filed in connection with the tragedy that affected villages in the Banda and Shahgarh tehsils, police have added 22 more people as accused, bringing the total number of accused in the cases to 52. Of these, 37 people have been arrested so far in police raids across various parts of the state, including Sagar, Morena, and Gwalior, officials said.
Sagar Superintendent of Police (SP) Anurag Sujania stated that the police also seized several items used in the manufacturing process of counterfeit liquor. These included 11,050 empty bottles, 900 bottles filled with such liquor, four dyes used to print brand labels, a machine used to seal liquor bottles, and large amounts of packaging raw materials. These items were seized during various raids.
The police had earlier arrested multiple people accused of being involved in a conspiracy to make and supply counterfeit liquor. The latest arrests include those accused of manufacturing the liquor and arranging raw materials. Among those in Sagar police custody is Anupam Giri, the owner of the Delhi-based RN Chemicals.
Two of the prime accused, Manish Lodhi and Sidhharth Kushwaha, both owners of government-licensed liquor shops and accused of supplying spurious liquor through their shops, continue to remain absconding. Mr. Sujania said various teams were working to nab the remaining accused.
The SP said the accused were making counterfeit liquor under the name of ‘Sagar Gold’, a popular liquor brand in the district. He added that the accused had been involved in making counterfeit liquor using toxic materials in several districts of the State in the past.
Largescale manufacturing
“During interrogation of the arrested accused, it came to light that this type of illegal liquor manufacturing activity has been carried out on a large scale in several districts in connivance with other people in the past. Since the sole objective of this gang was to make huge profits, they used to make fake and substandard liquor from whatever intoxicating liquid was easily available to them. They used to choose such places where so-called well-off strongmen had dominance, so that the common people could not get information about their activities,” Mr. Sujania said.
Sagar Additional SP Narendra Solanki told The Hindu that a gang from Morena, headed by key accused Dinesh Shivhare, had been called to manufacture counterfeit liquor in Sagar’s Tatarwara village by local accused persons such as Chandrabhan Rajput alias Chandu Raja, a Karni Sena leader.
Mr. Solanki said that it was Chandrabhan Rajput who had invited Shivhare and his associates to Banda to make the liquor in his village, after Shivanjay Rajput, a 21-year-old accused from Sagar, connected the two.
“Dinesh Shivhare and his associate Devendra Jatav had also consumed the liquor and fallen ill. Their associates admitted them to a private hospital in Sagar. But as soon as they realised that it was their liquor that caused this, they got Dinesh discharged and headed for Morena. He died on the way while Jatav lost his vision,” the Additional SP said.
Mr. Solanki said that based on the inputs from questioning, police teams were sent to Gwalior and Morena, where six accused, including Dinesh Shivhare’s brother Lalit Shivhare, were arrested and manufacturing items were recovered.
The Delhi connection
He said that an accused held from Morena, Bunty Sharma, who has been involved in making counterfeit liquor in the past, had connected Dinesh Shivhare to the chemical supplier in Delhi.
The officer said that the police had learnt that Shivanjay had gone to pick up five drums of a chemical at a local logistics warehouse in Sagar,
“When we investigated this lead, we traced the drums to Delhi. A team was then sent to Delhi. The logistics company there did not have the sender’s details, but we got the vehicle number from the CCTV footage and traced the driver, who then led us to Anupam Giri. He is currently being interrogated about his source and how long he has been supplying toxic chemicals for such uses,” Mr. Solanki said.
The tragedy in Sagar had come to light with the death of 11 people on September 6. The official death toll in the tragedy is 20, but local reports claim the number is higher. The tragedy has also caused partial to complete vision loss in several of those who consumed the liquor.

title: Ecologists urge scientists and policymakers to study imminent ‘Super’ El Niño to prepare for the future
text:
As many as 188 of India’s scientists and ecologists jointly published an appeal to fellow researchers and field practitioners to prepare for the effects of upcoming El Niño — a global weather phenomenon that dampens the monsoon and leads to extreme hot and dry conditions in the subcontinent.
In the Pacific Ocean where El Niño originates, temperatures have steadily risen above the 0.5°C threshold, reaching +2.6°C in August 2026. Projections report possible anomalies of up to +4°C, which is higher than at any time in the past 1,000 years, based on reconstructions from coral cores, they said.
Over the upcoming months, the signatories warned, India’s natural systems are likely to experience a range of potentially devastating impacts as a result of El Niño. “These include widespread bleaching and mortality of coral, an increase in wildfires, and the death of large rainforest trees. With a high probability of drought and extreme heat conditions, this year’s El Niño is likely to be catastrophic for India’s farmers, fishers and shepherds as well. In addition, though, more subtle impacts on India’s nature — including delayed fruit production or changes in animal behaviour — could be equally important, but may be much less visible unless you are specifically looking for them,” they said.
The ‘Call to Action’ urges scientists to take advantage of the warning signs and mobilise as a community to document and study the impact of this event on India’s nature, arguing that better science and documentation are essential to preparing India for a climate resilient future.
Jayashree Ratnam, Scientist, National Centre for Biological Sciences, said in a release: “The coming year will be a litmus test for tropical forests and trees in India. Huge forest trees may appear indestructible, but in the Western Ghats, many of them are already near the limit of the heat they can tolerate. Large trees are especially susceptible to extended droughts. Trees in cities are also vulnerable because of the urban ‘heat island’ effect. It is vital to understand how the coming El Niño will impact trees and other plants — as these are the foundations on which all other life depends.”
“I have witnessed the devastating impacts of El Niños on India’s coral reefs before, and it is heartbreaking. Coral reefs can be remarkably resilient, but they need at least a decade after every major die-back of coral to show significant recovery. The last major El Niño was in 2024, and barely two years after that event, the projected scale and intensity of the heat wave that is currently headed our way is truly scary,” said Rohan Arthur, Marine Biologist with Nature Conservation Foundation.
Roxy Mathew Koll, Climate Scientist with the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, also said India’s monsoon season is closing with a rainfall deficit, but the impacts may not end there. “They can creep into the seasons ahead and cascade through depleted soil moisture and water storage, land and marine heatwaves, stressed crops and livelihoods, forest fires, coral bleaching and less visible ecological changes. This gives us a short but valuable window to act. We must document these changes as they unfold, but also safeguard the ecosystems that remain and reduce the pressures already weakening them. What we learn and protect during this El Niño can help India prepare for a warmer and more volatile future.”

title: Bengaluru firm ropes in Israel’s P-Cure to launch network of compact proton therapy centres in India
text:
P-Cure Ltd., an Israeli medical technology company, and ARISTION Proton Center Private Limited, a Bengaluru-based healthcare infrastructure firm focused on advanced oncology and precision medicine, have entered into an agreement to build a network of compact proton therapy centres and dedicated proton therapy infrastructure across India at an investment ₹1,900 crore.
ARISTION Proton Center will deploy P-Cure’s compact, synchrotron-based proton therapy systems in India. The first such centre, a 660-bed quaternary campus built around integrated artificial intelligence and augmented care solutions, will come up Sentient Health City, at Jakkur, followed by similar centres in Kochi and in other cities, said the companies.
The companies said that proton therapy is a non-invasive type of radiation treatment that uses a beam of positively charged particles called protons to destroy cancer cells. Protons travel a precise distance and release a burst of energy right at the tumor site, unlike in the case of conventional radiation which passes all the way through the body and damages healthy tissue as well.
Lohith G. Reddy, CMD and radiation oncologist, ARISTION Proton Center, said, “India already delivers world-class medical care, but what has been missing is proton and ion precision treatment at the scale a nation of 1.4 billion deserves. P-Cure’s compact system gives us the economics to build not one showpiece facility but a national network, delivering the world’s most advanced radiation therapy at a cost structure Indian patients can actually access.’’
P-Cure CEO Michael Marash said, “India represents one of the most important growth frontiers for proton therapy, and this agreement is a milestone for P-Cure as we bring our technology to the country for the first time.’’

title: Creative minds exhibit engineering skills at graVITas’ 26 at VIT
text:

Divided into two categories (15kg and 60kg) based on the weight of the robot, those in the bout were remotely operated by a team outside the ring. A damaged robot in the ring should be repaired in 20 minutes to participate again but could not be replaced with a new robot.

The drones should not hit these obstacles. Drones that take lesser time to reach the finish line were declared winners. The key to success in the drone competition was to have small, weightless drones that can easily navigate the obstacles.
The competition also provided a platform for students to run their own startups. Titled as capital hunt, experienced investors in the startup industry were roped in to guide students on the nuances of running successful startups.

title: Govt. stays implementation of minimum marks in Keralam schools
text:
The government has decided to temporarily stay an order implementing minimum marks for classes VIII, IX, and X in the 2026-27 academic year.
Implementation of minimum marks was one of the most significant and debated decisions of the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government.
The LDF had in 2024 given approval for the implementation of 30% minimum marks in the theory component of each subject in school examinations as part of steps to enhance the quality of education. The decision was taken in the wake of criticism from many sections that students were not achieving the desired learning outcomes.
Despite opposition by the pro-CPI(M) Kerala School Teachers’ Association, Students’ Federation of India, and the Kerala Sastra Sahithya Parishad, the LDF government had begun implementing it in the 2024-25 academic year for class VIII students and in the 2025-26 year for class VIII and IX students. In the 2026-27 academic year, it was supposed to be be implemented for classes VIII to X.
Along with implementation of subject minimum, the then government had given thrust to strengthening continuous evaluation and making it merit based.
Also, a learning support programme was rolled out so that students who failed to secure 30% minimum marks in the annual examinations were given academic support and made to appear for the exams again.
However, most significantly students appearing for the SSLC examinations will not have to worry about securing minimum 30% marks in the theory component of each paper.
There are concerns that the decision to stay the implementation of minimum marks will have an adverse impact on education standards.
The Left-affiliated All Kerala School Teachers Union, in a statement, said that abandoning examination reforms, which were introduced to ensure that students attained learning outcomes and met academic standards, in the last phase when they were to be implemented in class X would destroy the trust in public education. No discussion had been held before taking the decision, AKSTU general secretary O.K. Jayakrishnan said, seeking a re-think on the staying of minimum mark implementation.

title: Seven of a family from Odisha among eight killed as car falls into drain in Madhya Pradesh
text:
Eight people, three children and two women among them, died on Saturday (September 19, 2026) after their car was swept away in a swollen drain in Madhya Pradesh’s Agar Malwa district. The victims were on their way to visit a temple in Nalkheda town.
According to the police, the incident took place in the early hours on Saturday (September 19) following a heavy overnight downpour in Nalkheda.
Agar Malwa Superintendent of Police Dilip Soni told The Hindu that seven of the deceased were from a family in Odisha and were on their way to visit the Bagalmukhi temple in Nalkheda, while the driver was a resident of the Badod tehsil area. He said that the accident took place just 50 metres from the temple.
“There is a culvert near the temple, and the drain under it had been overflowing due to heavy rain. The driver tried to cross it to reach the temple but may have misjudged the situation, after which the car lost control and got swept away due to strong currents,” Mr. Soni said, adding that the family had come to Nalkheda after visiting the Mahakaleshwar temple in Ujjain.
The police got information about a submerged car from local people around 9:30 a.m., after which the bodies were recovered, Mr. Soni said.
The police officer said that post-mortem examinations have been conducted on all the bodies, and those of the victims from Odisha have been dispatched to Bhubaneswar. The police have begun inquest proceedings in the case.
Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi expressed deep sorrow over the deaths. “The State government has instructed the officials concerned to maintain constant coordination with the Madhya Pradesh government and the local administration regarding the incident,” he said.
“All necessary steps are being taken... to bring the mortal remains back to Odisha with due respect. In this hour of grief, the State government stands firmly by the side of the bereaved families,” Mr. Majhi said.
In Bhubaneswar, a pall of gloom descended on the family of Banamali Behera, who lost his son, two daughters, a son-in-law, and three grandchildren in the accident. The family, originally from the Gadakana area of Bhubaneswar, ran a roadside eatery at the busy Jayadev Vihar Square. They were preparing to celebrate two auspicious occasions — a wedding in the family and moving into a new house. Mr. Behera’s daughter, Radharani Behera, 30, who was among the victims, was scheduled to have her ring ceremony on September 27 after the family returned from their trip. They had begun their journey on September 16.
Former Odisha Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik also expressed grief over the incident in a post on X. “I am deeply saddened to learn about the heartbreaking accident in Madhya Pradesh in which seven Odia devotees lost their lives. On this sorrowful occasion, I convey my deepest condolences to the bereaved family members and pray for the eternal peace of the departed souls,” he wrote.

title: Bengaluru passengers welcome government move against advance tipping, drivers seek fairer fares
text:
Passengers in Bengaluru have welcomed the Central Consumer Protection Authority’s (CCPA) action against pre-ride tipping prompts on ride-hailing platforms, saying the move could help curb what they describe as coercive pricing practices.
However, auto and cab drivers have raised concerns that the restriction could affect their daily earnings, particularly as aggregator platforms continue to charge significant commissions on trips.
The government has directed cab aggregators to stop offering advance tipping options before a ride is booked, describing the practice as misleading and unfair. Consumer Affairs Secretary Nidhi Khare made the statement on September 16, 2026, a day after the CCPA imposed a ₹10 lakh penalty on ride-hailing platform Rapido for several alleged unfair business practices, including the provision of advance tipping options.
The CCPA is also examining the business practices of other major ride-hailing platforms, including Uber and Ola.
In Bengaluru, some commuters said pre-ride tipping had increasingly become part of the booking experience, particularly when demand was high or drivers were reluctant to accept short-distance trips.
“It felt less like a tip and more like a bribe to get a ride. The government’s intervention brings transparency back to the baseline fare. However, I have been seeing major cab aggregators continuing to collect tips,” said Priya Rao, an auto commuter from J.P. Nagar.
Drivers seek fairer earnings
Shekhar Prasad from Whitefield said that he had experienced similar issues while trying to book an auto through multiple platforms. “Despite the government’s clear directions, they continue to show the tipping option. Yesterday, I was trying to book an auto through multiple apps, but after not getting one for almost half an hour, I had to offer a tip of more than ₹80 to get an auto,” he said.
Drivers, however, argue that the issue needs to be viewed in the context of their overall earnings. Auto and cab drivers have pointed to aggregator commissions, which they claim can account for around 25% to 30% of the trip value, along with rising fuel and maintenance costs and low-value short-distance rides.
Auto drivers said that they do not support manipulative app interfaces or practices that pressure passengers into tipping before a ride. At the same time, they want voluntary tipping after a trip to remain easily available to passengers.
“We are already losing a huge chunk of our hard-earned money to aggregator commissions. Tips directly benefit us without platform deductions. While banning pre-booking manipulation is fair, the system must ensure that post-ride tipping remains simple and accessible. If passengers are happy with the service, that extra amount belongs to the driver,” said T.M. Rudramurthy, general secretary of the Auto Rickshaw Drivers’ Union (ARDU).
Sustainable fare structure
Mr. Rudramurthy also called for a more sustainable fare structure based on regulated metered fares. “We believe the best approach would be to implement metered fares with a minimum fare of at least ₹40 in the city, along with an annual fare revision linked to inflation. This would provide a more sustainable fare structure for drivers while helping to reduce passengers’ dependence on app-based aggregators,” he added.
The Hindu tried to reach out to major cab aggregators for their reactions, but none responded.
